113	@dataclass
114	class BenchmarkResult:
115	    name: str
116	    score: float
117	    metric: str
118	    num_samples: int = 0
119	    per_sample: list[float] | None = None  # per-sample correctness (0/1) for paired stats
120	    raw: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
121	    command: str = ""  # the exact harness command that produced this result
122	    stats: Any = None  # optional TokenStats (agentic benchmarks); efficiency provenance
123	    turns: int = 0     # total agent turns spent (agentic benchmarks)
124	
125	    @classmethod
126	    def from_agent_result(cls, agent_result: Any, *, name: str,
127	                          metric: str = "resolved_rate") -> BenchmarkResult:
128	        """Bridge an ``AgentEvalResult`` into a benchmark row.
129	
130	        Carries the agentic score plus its efficiency provenance (token totals +
131	        turns), so an agentic benchmark folded into an :class:`EvalResult` lands
132	        in the reproducibility manifest's ``efficiency`` block automatically.
133	        """
134	        return cls(
135	            name=name,
136	            score=agent_result.mean_score(),
137	            metric=metric,
138	            num_samples=agent_result.num_scored(),
139	            per_sample=agent_result.per_sample() or None,
140	            stats=agent_result.token_totals(),
141	            turns=agent_result.total_turns(),
142	        )
143	
144	
145	@dataclass
146	class EvalResult:
147	    """Aggregated result of evaluating a model across one or more benchmarks."""
148	
149	    model: str
150	    backend: str
151	    benchmarks: dict[str, BenchmarkResult] = field(default_factory=dict)
152	    commands: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # exact eval commands executed
153	    healed: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)     # self-heal mutations applied
154	
155	    def add(self, result: BenchmarkResult) -> None:
156	        self.benchmarks[result.name] = result
157	        cmd = getattr(result, "command", "")
158	        if cmd and cmd not in self.commands:
159	            self.commands.append(cmd)
160	
161	    def mean_score(self) -> float:
162	        if not self.benchmarks:
163	            return 0.0
164	        return sum(b.score for b in self.benchmarks.values()) / len(self.benchmarks)
165	
166	    def efficiency(self) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
167	        """Token + turn totals across agentic benchmarks (``None`` if none carry any).
168	
169	        Only benchmarks produced by an agent (which attach a ``stats``/``turns``)
170	        contribute; a pure lm_eval run has no such provenance and yields ``None``.
171	        """
172	        from ..agent_eval.stats import TokenStats
173	
174	        tokens = TokenStats()
175	        total_turns = 0
176	        contributing = 0
177	        for b in self.benchmarks.values():
178	            if b.stats is not None:
179	                tokens.merge(b.stats)
180	            if b.turns:
181	                total_turns += b.turns
182	            if b.stats is not None or b.turns:
183	                contributing += 1
184	        if contributing == 0:
185	            return None
186	        eff: dict[str, Any] = {
187	            "num_benchmarks": contributing,
188	            "total_turns": total_turns,
189	        }
190	        if not tokens.is_empty():
191	            eff["tokens"] = tokens.to_dict()
192	        return eff
193	
194	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
195	        out: dict[str, Any] = {
196	            "model": self.model,
197	            "backend": self.backend,
198	            "mean_score": self.mean_score(),
199	            "results": {
200	                name: {"score": b.score, "metric": b.metric, "num_samples": b.num_samples}
201	                for name, b in self.benchmarks.items()
202	            },
203	            "commands": list(self.commands),
204	            "healed": list(self.healed),
205	        }
206	        eff = self.efficiency()
207	        if eff is not None:
208	            out["efficiency"] = eff
209	        return out
210	
211	
212	class BenchmarkRegistry:
213	    """Loads benchmark recipes from a directory (default: repo ``recipes/benchmarks``)."""
214	
215	    def __init__(self, root: Path | None = None):
216	        self.root = Path(root) if root else _RECIPE_ROOT
217	        self._cache: dict[str, BenchmarkRecipe] = {}
218	
219	    def _load_file(self, path: Path) -> BenchmarkRecipe:
220	        data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text()) or {}
221	        try:
222	            return BenchmarkRecipe.model_validate(data)
223	        except Exception as exc:
224	            raise RecipeError(f"invalid benchmark recipe {path}: {exc}") from exc
225	
226	    def load_all(self) -> dict[str, BenchmarkRecipe]:
227	        if self._cache:
228	            return dict(self._cache)
229	        if not self.root.exists():
230	            return {}
231	        for path in sorted(self.root.glob("*.yaml")):
232	            recipe = self._load_file(path)
233	            self._cache[recipe.name] = recipe
234	        return dict(self._cache)
235	
236	    def names(self) -> list[str]:
237	        return sorted(self.load_all())
238	
239	    def get(self, name: str) -> BenchmarkRecipe:
240	        recipes = self.load_all()
241	        if name in recipes:
242	            return recipes[name]
243	        # Fall back to a bare lm_eval task not covered by a recipe file.
244	        return BenchmarkRecipe(name=name, harness="lm_eval")

1	"""``aqa`` command-line interface.
2	
3	Verbs mirror NeMo Evaluator's ``nel``: run / eval / quant / validate / list /
4	compare / gate / report -- a clear, declarative surface over the pipeline.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import json
10	import sys
11	from pathlib import Path
12	
13	import click
14	
15	from . import __version__
16	from .config import load_run_config
17	from .eval.registry import BenchmarkRegistry
18	from .logging_util import AqaError, get_logger
19	from .registry import EXECUTORS, all_registries
20	
21	_log = get_logger("cli")
22	
23	
24	@click.group()
25	@click.version_option(__version__, prog_name="aqa")
26	def main() -> None:
27	    """autoquant-agent: agent-driven quantize / evaluate / self-heal."""
28	
29	
30	@main.command()
31	@click.argument("config", type=click.Path(exists=True, dir_okay=False))
32	@click.option("--dry-run", is_flag=True, help="Validate and print the plan without executing.")
33	@click.option("--resume", is_flag=True, help="Resume an interrupted run if detected.")
34	def run(config: str, dry_run: bool, resume: bool) -> None:
35	    """Run a full quantize -> evaluate -> gate pipeline from a run.yaml."""
36	    cfg = load_run_config(config)
37	    executor = EXECUTORS.create(cfg.executor.type, **cfg.executor.options)
38	    result = executor.run(cfg, dry_run=dry_run, resume=resume)
39	    click.echo(f"state={result.state.value} output={result.output_dir}")
40	
41	
42	@main.command()
43	@click.argument("config", type=click.Path(exists=True, dir_okay=False))
44	def validate(config: str) -> None:
45	    """Type-check + sanity-check a run.yaml (no execution)."""
46	    cfg = load_run_config(config)
47	    reg = BenchmarkRegistry()
48	    known = set(reg.names())
49	    unknown = [b for b in cfg.eval.benchmarks if b not in known]
50	    click.echo(f"OK: model={cfg.model} executor={cfg.executor.type} backend={cfg.eval.backend}")
51	    click.echo(f"    benchmarks={cfg.eval.benchmarks}")
52	    if unknown:
53	        click.echo(f"    note: no recipe file for {unknown} (will fall back to bare lm_eval tasks)")
54	    if cfg.executor.type not in EXECUTORS.names():
55	        raise click.ClickException(f"unknown executor {cfg.executor.type!r}")
56	    if cfg.eval.backend not in _backend_names():
57	        raise click.ClickException(f"unknown backend {cfg.eval.backend!r}")
58	
59	
60	@main.command()
61	@click.argument("dataset", type=click.Path(exists=True, dir_okay=False))
62	@click.option("--base-url", required=True, help="OpenAI-compatible endpoint of the served model.")
63	@click.option("--model", "served_model", required=True, help="Served model name (endpoint id).")
64	@click.option("--api-key-env", default=None, help="Env var holding the endpoint API key.")
65	@click.option("--out", type=click.Path(), default="./results/swebench", help="Output directory.")
66	@click.option("--limit", type=int, default=None, help="Cap the number of instances.")
67	@click.option("--instance-id", "instance_ids", multiple=True, help="Only these instance ids.")
68	@click.option("--difficulty", default=None, help="Only instances of this difficulty.")
69	@click.option("--concurrency", type=int, default=4, help="Instances graded in parallel.")
70	@click.option("--max-turns", type=int, default=40, help="ReAct turn budget per instance.")
71	@click.option("--scaffold", default="aqa-react",
72	              help="Agent scaffold / infra: aqa-react (default), codex, swe-agent.")
73	@click.option("--namespace", default="swebench", help="Docker namespace for eval images.")
74	def swebench(
75	    dataset: str, base_url: str, served_model: str, api_key_env: str | None, out: str,
76	    limit: int | None, instance_ids: tuple[str, ...], difficulty: str | None,
77	    concurrency: int, max_turns: int, scaffold: str, namespace: str,
78	) -> None:
79	    """Evaluate a served model on SWE-bench Verified (agentic, official scoring)."""
80	    import os
81	
82	    from .agent_eval.client import ModelClient
83	    from .swebench import load_swebench, run_swebench
84	    from .swebench.run import default_sandbox_factory
85	
86	    instances = load_swebench(
87	        dataset, instance_ids=list(instance_ids) or None,
88	        limit=limit, difficulty=difficulty)
89	    if not instances:
90	        raise click.ClickException("no SWE-bench instances selected")
91	    api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_env) if api_key_env else None
92	    client = ModelClient(base_url=base_url, model=served_model, api_key=api_key)
93	    _, report = run_swebench(
94	        instances, client, model_name=served_model, out_dir=out,
95	        concurrency=concurrency, max_turns=max_turns, scaffold=scaffold,
96	        sandbox_factory=default_sandbox_factory(namespace=namespace),
97	    )
98	    resolved = sum(1 for r in report.results if r.resolved)
99	    click.echo(f"SWE-bench: resolved {resolved}/{len(report.results)} "
100	               f"({100 * report.resolved_rate:.1f}%) -> {out}")
101	
102	
103	@main.command(name="list")
104	@click.option("--what", type=click.Choice(["benchmarks", "plugins", "all"]), default="all")
105	def list_cmd(what: str) -> None:
106	    """List available benchmarks and/or registered plugins."""
107	    if what in ("benchmarks", "all"):
108	        click.echo("benchmarks:")
109	        for name in BenchmarkRegistry().names():
110	            click.echo(f"  {name}")
111	    if what in ("plugins", "all"):
112	        click.echo("plugins:")
113	        for group, reg in all_registries().items():
114	            click.echo(f"  {group}: {', '.join(reg.names()) or '<none>'}")
115	
116	
117	@main.command()
118	@click.argument("config", type=click.Path(exists=True, dir_okay=False))
119	@click.option("--out", type=click.Path(), default="./results", help="Output directory.")
120	def eval(config: str, out: str) -> None:
121	    """Evaluate a model (no quantization) from a run.yaml, locally in-process."""
122	    from .eval.runner import run_evaluation
123	
124	    cfg = load_run_config(config)
125	    result = run_evaluation(cfg.model, cfg.eval, Path(out))
126	    click.echo(json.dumps(result.to_dict(), indent=2))
127	
128	
129	@main.command()
130	@click.argument("baseline", type=click.Path(exists=True))
131	@click.argument("candidate", type=click.Path(exists=True))
132	def compare(baseline: str, candidate: str) -> None:
133	    """Compare two accuracy.json result dirs/files and print score deltas."""
134	    b = _load_accuracy(baseline)
135	    c = _load_accuracy(candidate)
136	    click.echo(f"{'benchmark':<20}{'baseline':>10}{'candidate':>12}{'delta':>10}")
137	    for name in sorted(set(b) | set(c)):
138	        bs, cs = b.get(name), c.get(name)
139	        delta = (cs - bs) if (bs is not None and cs is not None) else float("nan")
140	        click.echo(f"{name:<20}{_fmt(bs):>10}{_fmt(cs):>12}{delta:>10.4f}")
141	
142	
143	def _fmt(v):
144	    return "-" if v is None else f"{v:.4f}"
145	
146	
147	def _load_accuracy(path: str) -> dict[str, float]:
148	    p = Path(path)
149	    if p.is_dir():
150	        p = p / "accuracy.json"
151	    data = json.loads(p.read_text())
152	    return {k: v.get("score") for k, v in data.get("results", {}).items()}
153	
154	
155	def _backend_names() -> list[str]:
156	    from .registry import BACKENDS
157	
158	    return BACKENDS.names()
159	
160	
161	def main_entry() -> None:  # pragma: no cover
162	    try:
163	        main()
164	    except AqaError as exc:
165	        click.echo(f"error: {exc}", err=True)
166	        sys.exit(1)
167	
168	
169	if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover
170	    main_entry()

1	"""Agent-optimize: analyse a model and let an agent propose an optimal auto-round command.
2	
3	Ports ``local_dispatch/agent/agent_optimize.py`` into the framework.  The flow:
4	
5	  1. :func:`analyze_model` -- download-free structure analysis (config.json + the
6	     safetensors index *names only*, so even huge MoE models are cheap).
7	  2. :func:`build_optimize_prompt` -- ask the agent for ONE ``auto-round`` command.
8	  3. :func:`extract_command` + :func:`validate_command` -- parse the agent's answer
9	     and enforce safety (never FP-protect routed-expert weights; exact output dir).
10	  4. :func:`run_agent_optimize` -- orchestrate (analyse -> agent -> extract/validate),
11	     returning a validated command or ``None`` (caller falls back to the deterministic
12	     builder, so this can only help, never block, a run).
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import json
18	import re
19	import shlex
20	import struct
21	from collections.abc import Callable
22	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
23	from pathlib import Path
24	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
25	
26	from ..logging_util import get_logger
27	from .tiers import Tier
28	
29	if TYPE_CHECKING:
30	    from ..config import QuantConfig
31	
32	_log = get_logger("agent.optimize")
33	
34	_LAYER_IDX_RE = re.compile(r"\.\d+\.")
35	_TRAIL_IDX_RE = re.compile(r"\.\d+$")
36	_CMD_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(r"```(?:autoround-cmd|bash|sh)?\s*\n(.*?)```", re.DOTALL)
37	
38	# Structured recipe document the agent is asked to produce.  Ported from
39	# ``local_dispatch/agent/agent_optimize.py`` -- the readable 8-section analysis is
40	# what makes the recommendation auditable/intuitive (not just a bare command).
41	RECIPE_DOC_TEMPLATE = """# <model> AutoRound Quantization Recipe
42	
43	## 1. TL;DR
44	- Recommended scheme / method(iters) / export format, one-line rationale each
45	- Expected accuracy-retention rate
46	- Final command: see section 6
47	
48	## 2. Model structure analysis
49	- Architecture / model_type / parameter scale / layer count
50	- Dense vs MoE (expert count, experts-per-token, fused 3-D expert or not)
51	- Attention type: MHA / GQA / MLA(latent) / linear(Mamba) / sparse(DSA/indexer)
52	- Actual router/gate module names (from the safetensors index)
53	- Special modules: shared_experts / MTP / multimodal(vision/mm_projector) / indexer
54	
55	## 3. Module-name inventory (safetensors index, de-indexed)
56	- Global / attention / MLP(dense) / MLP(MoE experts) / router / special prefixes
57	
58	## 4. AutoRound built-in handling for this structure
59	- Layers this model_type auto-ignores/special-cases (e.g. `.gate` routers)
60	
61	## 5. Quantization config decision
62	- scheme rationale (MXFP4 vs MXFP4_RCEIL vs MXFP8 vs W4A16/W8A16; MoE often RCEIL)
63	- iters / method (RTN=0 / tuning=200 / model_free) vs model scale
64	- Layers to KEEP FP16 with per-item rationale: lm_head, embedding, router/gate,
65	  self_attn (MLA or FP4 case), shared_experts, vision_tower/mm_projector, linear_attn
66	- layer_config mixed precision (e.g. experts->MXFP4, sensitive layers->MXFP8)
67	- Quantization target confirmed: routed experts MUST be quantized (bulk of params)
68	- Operator-fixed config review: for EACH hard constraint, confirm the command
69	  honors it and state whether you agree; if you'd recommend a different value,
70	  say so here as advice (the command still obeys the operator).
71	
72	## 6. Recommended command (auto_round CLI mode)
73	```autoround-cmd
74	auto-round --model_name <model> --scheme ... --output_dir <REQUIRED> --format ... ...
75	```
76	
77	## 7. Accuracy expectation & validation
78	- Expected retention, validation method (lm-eval vs BF16 baseline)
79	
80	## 8. Optional variants & caveats
81	- More aggressive / more conservative options; known pitfalls (ignore-name vs actual
82	  weight-name mismatch causing load errors, etc.)
83	- If any operator-fixed value looks suboptimal for this model, record your
84	  recommended alternative here (advisory only — the command above still obeys it).
85	"""
86	
87	# Concrete auto_round CLI exemplars (tuning / model_free / mixed-precision).  Always
88	# pass the model via ``--model_name`` (this auto-round build mis-parses positional).
89	CLI_EXAMPLES = """### Example A -- MoE mixed precision + tuning (experts MXFP4, rest MXFP8)
90	```bash
91	auto-round --model_name <MODEL> --iters 200 --scheme MXFP8 \\
92	  --ignore_layers vision_tower,lm_head,block_sparse_moe.gate,embed_tokens,self_attn,multi_modal_projector \\
93	  --layer_config "{mlp.experts:{bits:4,data_type:mx_fp}}" \\
94	  --format llm_compressor --output_dir <OUT> --device_map auto
95	```
96	
97	### Example B -- huge MoE, pure RTN (iters=0), MXFP4_RCEIL
98	```bash
99	auto-round --model_name <MODEL> --scheme MXFP4_RCEIL --iters 0 \\
100	  --fp_layers lm_head,mlp.gate,self_attn \\
101	  --format llm_compressor --output_dir <OUT> --device_map auto
102	```
103	
104	### Example C -- model_free (no model load, cheapest; fp8 source or NON-pre-packed huge weights)
105	# NOTE: model_free only dequantizes fp8 sources. NEVER use --model_free when the
106	# MoE experts are already MXFP4-packed (weights named `*_blocks`/`*_scales`, e.g.
107	# gpt-oss): it cannot dequant that native layout and emits a broken checkpoint.
108	# For such models use the model-load path (no --model_free) + --iters 0 (RTN).
109	```bash

192	def _tensor_names(model_id: str, revision: str, token: str | None, *,
193	                  index_file: str = "model.safetensors.index.json",
194	                  single_file: str = "model.safetensors") -> list[str]:
195	    """Tensor names from the safetensors index (no weights); fall back to a header read."""
196	    from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
197	    try:
198	        from huggingface_hub.utils import EntryNotFoundError
199	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
200	        EntryNotFoundError = Exception  # type: ignore[assignment,misc]
201	    try:
202	        idx = hf_hub_download(model_id, index_file, revision=revision, token=token)
203	        return sorted(json.loads(Path(idx).read_text()).get("weight_map", {}).keys())
204	    except EntryNotFoundError:

206	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
207	        _log.debug("index read failed, trying header: %s", exc)
208	    try:
209	        path = hf_hub_download(model_id, single_file, revision=revision, token=token)
210	        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
211	            (n,) = struct.unpack("<Q", fh.read(8))
212	            header = json.loads(fh.read(n))
213	        return sorted(k for k in header if k != "__metadata__")
214	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
215	        return []

218	def analyze_model(model_id: str, *, revision: str = "main",
219	                  token: str | None = None) -> ModelAnalysis:
220	    """Download-free structural analysis of a HF model (config + index names only)."""
221	    res = ModelAnalysis(model_id=model_id)
222	    index_file, single_file = "model.safetensors.index.json", "model.safetensors"
223	    try:
224	        cfg = _hf_config(model_id, revision, token)
225	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
226	        # Diffusion pipelines carry no root config.json; the quantization target
227	        # (transformer/unet) has its own config in a subfolder.
228	        if not _has_model_index(model_id, revision, token):
229	            res.ok = False
230	            res.error = f"config.json unavailable: {exc}"
231	            return res
232	        res.is_diffusion = True
233	        try:
234	            cfg = _hf_config(model_id, revision, token,
235	                             filename="transformer/config.json")
236	        except Exception as exc2:  # noqa: BLE001
237	            res.ok = False
238	            res.error = f"transformer/config.json unavailable: {exc2}"
239	            return res
240	        index_file = "transformer/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors.index.json"
241	        single_file = "transformer/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors"
242	
243	    res.architectures = list(cfg.get("architectures", []) or [])
244	    res.model_type = cfg.get("model_type", "") or ""
245	    for k in MOE_CONFIG_KEYS:
246	        v = cfg.get(k)
247	        if isinstance(v, int) and v > 1:
248	            res.is_moe = True
249	            res.num_experts = res.num_experts or v
250	    arch_str = " ".join(res.architectures).lower()
251	    if not res.is_moe and any(t in arch_str for t in ("moe", "sparse", "mixtral", "grok")):
252	        res.is_moe = True
253	    res.num_layers = cfg.get("num_hidden_layers") or cfg.get("n_layer") or cfg.get("num_layers")
254	    if any(cfg.get(k) for k in ("kv_lora_rank", "q_lora_rank", "qk_rope_head_dim")):
255	        res.has_mla = True
256	
257	    norm = sorted({_normalize(n) for n in _tensor_names(
258	        model_id, revision, token, index_file=index_file, single_file=single_file)})
259	    res.sample_modules = norm[:60]
260	    routers: set[str] = set()
261	    for m in norm:
262	        low = m.lower()
263	        if (m.endswith((".gate.weight", ".router.gate.weight")) or ".router" in low
264	                or m.split(".")[-1] == "gate") and "gate_proj" not in low:
265	            res.has_router = True
266	            routers.add(_rel(m))
267	        if "shared_expert" in low:
268	            res.has_shared_experts = True
269	        if "self_attn" in low or ".attn." in low:
270	            res.has_self_attn = True
271	        if any(v in low for v in ("vision", "visual", "multi_modal", "mm_projector",
272	                                  "image_", "vit")):
273	            res.has_vision = True
274	    res.router_names = sorted(routers)[:12]
275	    return res

368	def extract_command(log_text: str) -> str | None:
369	    """Pull the last ``auto-round`` command from the agent's output (code block first)."""
370	    candidates: list[str] = []
371	    for m in _CMD_BLOCK_RE.finditer(log_text or ""):
372	        body = re.sub(r"\\\s*\n\s*", " ", m.group(1).strip())
373	        for line in body.splitlines():
374	            line = line.strip().lstrip("$ ").strip()
375	            if line.startswith(("auto-round", "auto_round")):
376	                candidates.append(line)
377	                break
378	    if not candidates:
379	        joined = re.sub(r"\\\s*\n\s*", " ", log_text or "")
380	        for line in joined.splitlines():
381	            s = line.strip().lstrip("$ ").strip()
382	            if s.startswith(("auto-round", "auto_round")):
383	                candidates.append(s)
384	    return candidates[-1] if candidates else None

396	def ensure_model_name(cmd: str, model: str) -> str:
397	    """Guarantee the command carries an explicit ``--model_name <value>``."""
398	    try:
399	        toks = shlex.split(cmd)
400	    except ValueError:
401	        return cmd
402	    if not toks:
403	        return cmd
404	    head, rest = toks[0], toks[1:]
405	    flags = ("--model_name", "--model", "--model_name_or_path")
406	    model_val: str | None = None
407	    out: list[str] = []
408	    i = 0
409	    while i < len(rest):
410	        t = rest[i]
411	        if t in flags:
412	            nxt = rest[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(rest) else None
413	            if nxt is not None and not nxt.startswith("-"):
414	                model_val = model_val or nxt
415	                i += 2
416	                continue
417	            i += 1
418	            continue
419	        if "=" in t and t.split("=", 1)[0] in flags:
420	            v = t.split("=", 1)[1]
421	            if v and not v.startswith("-"):
422	                model_val = model_val or v
423	            i += 1
424	            continue
425	        out.append(t)
426	        i += 1
427	    if model_val is None:
428	        if model in out:
429	            out.remove(model)
430	            model_val = model
431	        elif out and not out[0].startswith("-"):
432	            model_val = out.pop(0)
433	        else:
434	            model_val = model
435	    out = [t for t in out if t != model_val]
436	    return " ".join(shlex.quote(t) for t in [head, "--model_name", model_val, *out])

448	@dataclass(frozen=True)
449	class QuantConstraint:
450	    """One operator-fixed recipe constraint the agent's command MUST satisfy.
451	
452	    Derived from the fields the user *explicitly set* in ``quant:`` (pydantic
453	    ``model_fields_set``) so agent-optimize augments rather than overrides the
454	    operator's intent. ``kind`` drives both the prompt directive and validation:
455	
456	    * ``value``   -- ``--flag`` must equal ``value`` (case-insensitive).
457	    * ``present`` -- boolean ``--flag`` must be present.
458	    * ``absent``  -- ``--flag`` must NOT appear (e.g. forbid ``--model_free``).
459	    * ``subset``  -- every comma token in ``value`` must appear in the flag's list.
460	    * ``haskeys`` -- the flag's value must contain each comma-listed key.
461	    """
462	
463	    label: str          # human directive rendered into the prompt
464	    flag: str           # auto-round flag it maps to
465	    kind: str           # value | present | absent | subset | haskeys
466	    value: str = ""     # expected value / comma tokens / keys (per ``kind``)
467	
468	    def satisfied_by(self, toks: list[str]) -> bool:
469	        present = self.flag in toks or any(t.startswith(self.flag + "=") for t in toks)
470	        if self.kind == "present":
471	            return present
472	        if self.kind == "absent":
473	            return not present
474	        got = _opt(toks, self.flag)
475	        if self.kind == "value":
476	            return got is not None and got.strip().lower() == self.value.strip().lower()
477	        if self.kind == "subset":
478	            if got is None:
479	                return False
480	            have = {x.strip() for x in got.split(",") if x.strip()}
481	            want = {x.strip() for x in self.value.split(",") if x.strip()}
482	            return want.issubset(have)
483	        if self.kind == "haskeys":
484	            return got is not None and all(k in got for k in self.value.split(",") if k)
485	        return True
486

488	def build_quant_constraints(quant_cfg: QuantConfig) -> list[QuantConstraint]:
489	    """Translate the user's *explicitly set* quant fields into hard constraints.
490	
491	    Only fields present in ``model_fields_set`` are enforced, so schema defaults
492	    never override the agent's structural analysis -- but anything the operator
493	    actually typed takes precedence over the agent's own recommendation.
494	    """
495	    setf = getattr(quant_cfg, "model_fields_set", set())
496	    cons: list[QuantConstraint] = []
497	
498	    if "scheme" in setf:
499	        cons.append(QuantConstraint(
500	            f"scheme MUST be `{quant_cfg.scheme}`", "--scheme", "value", quant_cfg.scheme))
501	    if "method" in setf:
502	        if quant_cfg.method == "model_free":
503	            cons.append(QuantConstraint(
504	                "MUST use the calibration-free model_free path (pass `--model_free`)",
505	                "--model_free", "present"))
506	        else:
507	            cons.append(QuantConstraint(
508	                "MUST use the model-load path -- do NOT pass `--model_free`",
509	                "--model_free", "absent"))
510	    if "export_format" in setf:
511	        cons.append(QuantConstraint(
512	            f"export/--format MUST be `{quant_cfg.export_format}`",
513	            "--format", "value", quant_cfg.export_format))
514	    if "iters" in setf and quant_cfg.iters is not None:
515	        cons.append(QuantConstraint(
516	            f"MUST pass `--iters {quant_cfg.iters}`", "--iters", "value", str(quant_cfg.iters)))
517	    if "nsamples" in setf and quant_cfg.nsamples is not None:
518	        cons.append(QuantConstraint(
519	            f"MUST pass `--nsamples {quant_cfg.nsamples}`",
520	            "--nsamples", "value", str(quant_cfg.nsamples)))
521	    if "ignore_layers" in setf and quant_cfg.ignore_layers:
522	        cons.append(QuantConstraint(
523	            f"`--ignore_layers` MUST include: {quant_cfg.ignore_layers}",
524	            "--ignore_layers", "subset", quant_cfg.ignore_layers))
525	    if "layer_config" in setf and quant_cfg.layer_config:
526	        keys = ",".join(str(k) for k in quant_cfg.layer_config)
527	        cons.append(QuantConstraint(
528	            f"`--layer_config` MUST cover keys: {keys}", "--layer_config", "haskeys", keys))
529	    if "algorithm" in setf and quant_cfg.algorithm:
530	        cons.append(QuantConstraint(
531	            f"`--algorithm` MUST be `{quant_cfg.algorithm}`",
532	            "--algorithm", "value", quant_cfg.algorithm))
533	    if "enable_alg_ext" in setf and quant_cfg.enable_alg_ext:
534	        cons.append(QuantConstraint(
535	            "MUST pass `--enable_alg_ext`", "--enable_alg_ext", "present"))
536	    if "hadamard_type" in setf and quant_cfg.hadamard_type:
537	        cons.append(QuantConstraint(
538	            f"`--rotation-hadamard-type` MUST be `{quant_cfg.hadamard_type}`",
539	            "--rotation-hadamard-type", "value", quant_cfg.hadamard_type))
540	    if "opt_rtn" in setf and quant_cfg.opt_rtn is not None:
541	        flag = "--enable_opt_rtn" if quant_cfg.opt_rtn else "--disable_opt_rtn"
542	        cons.append(QuantConstraint(f"MUST pass `{flag}`", flag, "present"))
543	    if "quant_lm_head" in setf and quant_cfg.quant_lm_head:
544	        cons.append(QuantConstraint(
545	            "MUST pass `--quant_lm_head`", "--quant_lm_head", "present"))
546	    return cons

549	def validate_command(cmd: str, a: ModelAnalysis, output_dir: str,
550	                     constraints: list[QuantConstraint] | None = None) -> tuple[bool, str]:
551	    """Return ``(ok, reason)``; enforce operator-fixed config + expert-safety."""
552	    try:
553	        toks = shlex.split(cmd)
554	    except ValueError as exc:
555	        return False, f"unparseable command: {exc}"
556	    if not toks or toks[0] not in ("auto-round", "auto_round"):
557	        return False, "command must start with auto-round"
558	    if _opt(toks, "--output_dir") != output_dir:
559	        return False, f"--output_dir must be exactly {output_dir}"
560	    if not (_opt(toks, "--model_name") or _opt(toks, "--model")
561	            or (len(toks) >= 2 and not toks[1].startswith("-"))):
562	        return False, "missing model (positional path or --model_name)"
563	
564	    # Operator-fixed config wins: reject any command that violates an explicit
565	    # user quant setting (so agent-optimize augments, never overrides, intent).
566	    for con in constraints or ():
567	        if not con.satisfied_by(toks):
568	            return False, f"violates operator-fixed config: {con.label}"
569	
570	    layer_cfg = _opt(toks, "--layer_config") or ""
571	    experts_reenabled = "expert" in layer_cfg.lower()
572	    protected = [
573	        x.strip()
574	        for x in ((_opt(toks, "--fp_layers") or "") + "," +
575	                  (_opt(toks, "--ignore_layers") or "")).split(",")
576	        if x.strip()
577	    ]
578	    if a.is_moe and not experts_reenabled:
579	        nuking = [t for t in protected if _protects_experts(t)]
580	        if nuking:
581	            return False, (f"would fp-protect routed experts {nuking} without a "
582	                           "--layer_config experts override")
583	        if protected and not any(("gate" in t or "router" in t) for t in protected):
584	            return False, "MoE run must fp-protect the router/gate"
585	    return True, "ok"

595	def save_recipe_doc(log_text: str, path: Path, model_id: str) -> None:
596	    """Persist the agent's Markdown recipe document (trims chatter before the H1)."""
597	    text = log_text or ""
598	    if text.lstrip().startswith("# "):
599	        i = text.find("# ")
600	    else:
601	        i = text.find("\n# ")
602	    if i != -1:
603	        text = text[i:]
604	    text = _VERDICT_TAIL_RE.sub("\n", text)
605	    header = (f"<!-- Auto-generated quantization recipe for {model_id} "
606	              f"by aqa agent-optimize. -->\n\n")
607	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
608	    path.write_text(header + text.strip() + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

611	def run_agent_optimize(
612	    model: str,
613	    *,
614	    scheme: str,
615	    method: str,
616	    export_format: str,
617	    output_dir: str,
618	    tier: Tier,
619	    run_agent: OptimizeAgentRunner,
620	    revision: str = "main",
621	    token: str | None = None,
622	    skill_recipe: str = "",
623	    user_context: str = "",
624	    recipe_knowledge: str | None = None,
625	    constraints: list[QuantConstraint] | None = None,
626	    log_dir: Path | None = None,
627	) -> str | None:
628	    """Analyse the model, ask the agent for a command, validate it; None on any miss."""
629	    a = analyze_model(model, revision=revision, token=token)
630	    if not a.ok:
631	        _log.warning("agent-optimize: analysis failed: %s", a.error)
632	        return None
633	    if recipe_knowledge is None:
634	        recipe_knowledge = load_recipe_knowledge(include_diffusion=a.is_diffusion)
635	    prompt = build_optimize_prompt(
636	        a, scheme=scheme, method=method, export_format=export_format,
637	        output_dir=output_dir, skill_recipe=skill_recipe, user_context=user_context,
638	        recipe_knowledge=recipe_knowledge, constraints=constraints,
639	    )
640	    log_dir = Path(log_dir or Path.cwd())
641	    log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
642	    log_path = log_dir / "optimize.log"
643	    output = run_agent(tier, prompt, log_path, f"optimize_{model.split('/')[-1]}")
644	    # A shared agent runner may hand back a structured outcome (fix-loop's
645	    # AgentOutcome) rather than a bare str; we only need its text for extraction.
646	    output = getattr(output, "text", output)
647	
648	    # Persist the human-readable recipe doc regardless of command validity -- the
649	    # structured analysis is valuable for auditing even when the command is rejected.
650	    try:
651	        save_recipe_doc(output, log_dir / "quantization_recipe.md", model)
652	        _log.info("agent-optimize: recipe doc -> %s", log_dir / "quantization_recipe.md")
653	    except OSError as exc:
654	        _log.warning("agent-optimize: could not save recipe doc (%s)", exc)
655	
656	    cmd = extract_command(output)
657	    if not cmd:
658	        _log.warning("agent-optimize: no auto-round command produced")
659	        return None
660	    cmd = ensure_model_name(cmd, model)
661	    ok, reason = validate_command(cmd, a, output_dir, constraints)
662	    if not ok:
663	        _log.warning("agent-optimize: rejected command (%s)", reason)
664	        return None
665	    _log.info("agent-optimize: validated command")
666	    return cmd

1	"""Agent fix-loop state machine.
2	
3	Ports ``agent_fix_loop`` from ``local_dispatch/agent/agent_fix_loop.sh`` into
4	Python.  The *orchestration* (tier escalation, drift detection, verdict handling,
5	progress override, lessons) lives here; the *execution* of a phase and the *agent
6	CLI call* are injected callables so the loop is fully unit-testable and reusable
7	by any phase (quantize / evaluate).
8	
9	Escalation triggers, faithful to the original:
10	  * ``VERDICT: UNFIXABLE`` -> escalate if a stronger tier exists, else give up.
11	  * ``VERDICT: ESCALATE``  -> escalate if a stronger tier exists.
12	  * drift (same error_class ``drift_threshold`` times in a row) -> escalate/abort.
13	  * per-tier ``tier_attempt_budget`` exhausted -> fail-safe escalate.
14	  * global ``max_attempts`` (auto-raised to tiers x budget) -> abort.
15	Deeper quant progress (a later ``layers.N``) resets drift -- real progress is never drift.
16	"""

125	def default_agent_runner(timeout: int) -> AgentRunner:
126	    def _runner(tier: Tier, prompt: str, log_path: Path, session_id: str) -> AgentOutcome:
127	        rc = -1
128	        try:
129	            rc = run_agent_fix(tier, prompt, log_path, session_id=session_id, timeout=timeout)
130	        except AgentUnavailable as exc:
131	            log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
132	            log_path.write_text(f"[agent-unavailable] {exc}\n")
133	            _log.warning("tier %s unavailable: %s", tier.name, exc)
134	        text = log_path.read_text() if log_path.exists() else ""
135	        return AgentOutcome(text=text, rc=rc, timed_out=(rc == TIMEOUT_RC))
136	    return _runner

142	    def __init__(
143	        self,
144	        phase_name: str,

147	        config: FixLoopConfig | None = None,
148	        out_dir: Path | None = None,

187	    def _effective_class(self, analysis: AgentAnalysis, err_text: str) -> str:
188	        if analysis.error_class and analysis.error_class != "unknown":
189	            return analysis.error_class

192	    def _same_error(self, cur_class: str, prev_class: str,
193	                    cur_text: str, prev_text: str) -> bool | None:
194	        """True/False if we can tell attempts share the same error, else None."""
195	        if (cur_class and cur_class != "unknown"
196	                and prev_class and prev_class != "unknown"):
197	            return cur_class == prev_class
198	        if prev_text:
199	            sim = logs_similarity(cur_text, prev_text)
200	            if sim is None:

202	            return sim >= 0.90

238	    @staticmethod

240	        """Record one attempt's hypothesis as a compact 'class: root_cause' line."""
241	        cls = (analysis.error_class or "").strip()
242	        cause = (analysis.root_cause or analysis.fix_plan or "").strip()

250	    def _make_prior(self, attempt: int, outcome: AgentOutcome,
251	                    analysis: AgentAnalysis, result: PhaseResult) -> PriorAttempt:
252	        """Snapshot the attempt that just ran, for injection into the next one.
253	
254	        ``result`` is the authoritative state AFTER this attempt (the fix-loop's own
255	        ``run_phase`` re-run, or the pre-attempt failure on a punt/escalate path) --
256	        the single signal the agent's own transcript never contains.

262	            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - diff is best-effort

265	            attempt=attempt,
266	            agent_verdict=(analysis.verdict.name if analysis.verdict else ""),
267	            agent_summary=(analysis.root_cause or analysis.fix_plan or "").strip()[:200],
268	            actual_ok=result.ok,
269	            actual_class=classify_error(result.log_text),
270	            truncated=outcome.timed_out,

274	    def _prior_attempt_files(self, attempt: int) -> list[str]:
275	        """Existing artifact files for ``attempt`` the next agent may read for depth."""
276	        stem = f"attempt_{attempt}"
277	        candidates = [
278	            f"{stem}.share.md",         # copilot human-readable transcript
279	            f"{stem}.events.jsonl",     # copilot structured session (survives truncation)
280	            f"{stem}.session.jsonl",    # openclaw structured session
281	            f"{stem}.log",              # streamed stdout (may be truncated)

287	    def _format_prior_state(self, prior: PriorAttempt | None) -> str:
288	        """Render the prior attempt into the prompt's high-priority state block."""
289	        if prior is None:
290	            return ""
291	        verdict = prior.agent_verdict or "<none -- output truncated>"
292	        lines = [
293	            f"- agent self-report: {verdict}"
294	            + (f" / plan: {prior.agent_summary}" if prior.agent_summary else ""),
295	        ]
296	        if prior.actual_ok:
297	            lines.append("- ACTUAL re-run (authoritative, the fix-loop verified this): PASSED")
298	        else:
299	            cls = f", error_class={prior.actual_class}" if prior.actual_class else ""
300	            lines.append(
301	                "- ACTUAL re-run (authoritative, the fix-loop verified this): STILL FAILING"
302	                f"{cls} -- so the previous attempt did NOT resolve it; do not just repeat it")
303	        if prior.truncated:
304	            lines.append("- timed out / truncated: YES -- edits may be HALF-APPLIED; reconcile "
305	                         "against the diff below before continuing (do not blindly redo them)")
306	        files = self._prior_attempt_files(prior.attempt)
307	        if files:
308	            lines.append("- full record of that attempt (READ these if you need its reasoning / "
309	                         "tool calls / evidence): " + ", ".join(files))
310	        return "\n".join(lines)

336	    def _record_trajectory(self, err_text: str, analysis: AgentAnalysis,

342	        """
343	        if self.knowledge is None:
344	            return
345	        rejected = trail[:-1] if trail else []
346	        try:

348	                self.phase_name, err_text, analysis,
349	                tried_and_rejected=rejected, tier=tier, steps=steps,

357	    def _replay_reference(self, error_text: str, *, max_candidates: int = 2,
358	                          inline_threshold: int = 1500, total_budget: int = 3000) -> str:
359	        """Format recorded fixes for THIS failure as agent *reference* (Option A).
360	
361	        We deliberately do NOT auto-apply recorded patches: a diff captured on a
362	        different model/checkpoint can silently break the environment, and the
363	        revert path is itself risky. Instead the best-matching recorded diffs +
364	        their provenance are handed to the agent, which decides whether the
365	        mechanism applies to the current model/checkpoint and adapts or ignores it.
366	
367	        To keep the prompt lean, only SMALL diffs are inlined; a large (e.g.
368	        multi-file source) patch is summarised (files touched, +/- line counts)
369	        with a pointer to its on-disk path for the agent to read on demand -- never
370	        hard-truncated mid-hunk. A running ``total_budget`` caps inlined bytes so
371	        two large candidates cannot both bloat the prompt. Returns "" when replay
372	        is disabled, there is no knowledge store, or nothing matches.
373	        """
374	        if not (self.replay and self.knowledge):
375	            return ""
376	        try:
377	            records = self.knowledge.find_patches(self.phase_name, error_text)
378	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - lookup is best-effort
379	            _log.warning("replay: lookup failed: %s", exc)
380	            return ""
381	        blocks: list[str] = []
382	        remaining = total_budget
383	        for rec in records[:max_candidates]:
384	            prov = (f"model={rec.model_id or '?'} scheme={rec.scheme or '?'} "
385	                    f"class={rec.error_class or '?'} sig={rec.sig_hash}")
386	            diff = rec.diff_text(max_chars=inline_threshold + 1)
387	            if diff and len(diff) <= inline_threshold and len(diff) <= remaining:
388	                remaining -= len(diff)
389	                blocks.append(f"### candidate ({prov})\n```diff\n{diff}\n```")
390	            else:
391	                # Too big to inline: summarise + point the agent at the patch on disk.
392	                paths = ", ".join(rec.patch_paths())
393	                blocks.append(
394	                    f"### candidate ({prov})\n{rec.stat_summary()}\n"
395	                    f"full patch on disk (READ it if the mechanism looks relevant): {paths}")
396	        if not blocks:
397	            return ""
398	        _log.info("replay: injecting %d recorded fix(es) as reference for %s "
399	                  "(no auto-apply)", len(blocks), self.phase_name)
400	        return "\n\n".join(blocks)
401	
402	    def _log_stat(self, outcome: str, *, sig_hash: str = "", error_class: str = "",
403	                  tier: str = "") -> None:
404	        if self.knowledge is None:
405	            return
406	        try:
407	            self.knowledge.log_event(self.phase_name, outcome, sig_hash=sig_hash,
408	                                     error_class=error_class, model_id=self.model_id,
409	                                     tier=tier)
410	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - telemetry is best-effort
411	            _log.warning("knowledge: stat log failed: %s", exc)

413	    # -- main loop -------------------------------------------------------
414	    def run(self) -> FixResult:
415	        """Drive the phase to success, stamping best-effort self-heal token usage."""
416	        from ..agent_eval.stats import TokenStats
417	        self._heal_tokens = TokenStats()
418	        fr = self._run_loop()
419	        if not self._heal_tokens.is_empty():
420	            fr.tokens = self._heal_tokens
421	        return fr
422	
423	    def _run_loop(self) -> FixResult:
424	        cfg = self.cfg
425	        self.fix_log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
426	
427	        tier_count = len(self.tiers)
428	        tier_idx = 0
429	        attempts_on_tier = 0
430	        drift_count = 0
431	        max_progress = -1
432	        prev_class = ""
433	        # Distilled record of hypotheses tried on the way to a fix; on success the
434	        # entries before the winner become the trajectory's "dead ends".
435	        rejected_trail: list[str] = []
436	        prev_text = ""
437	        prior: PriorAttempt | None = None  # distilled state of the previous attempt
438	
439	        # Ensure the global cap lets every tier reach its budget.
440	        max_attempts = max(cfg.max_attempts, tier_count * cfg.tier_attempt_budget)
441	
442	        cuda_was_available = bool(self.cuda_guard()) if self.cuda_guard else False
443	
444	        # Pristine snapshot BEFORE any run/edit so agent source changes become patches.
445	        if self.patch_capture is not None:
446	            try:
447	                self.patch_capture.snapshot()
448	            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - patch capture is best-effort
449	                _log.warning("patch snapshot failed: %s", exc)
450	
451	        _log.info("phase %s: initial run", self.phase_name)
452	        result = self.run_phase()
453	        if result.ok:
454	            _log.info("phase %s succeeded on first run", self.phase_name)
455	            return FixResult(ok=True, attempts=0, tier_index=0)
456	
457	        _log.warning("phase %s failed; entering fix loop (tiers=%s)",
458	                     self.phase_name, [t.name for t in self.tiers])
459	
460	        attempt = 0
461	        while attempt < max_attempts:
462	            attempt += 1
463	            attempts_on_tier += 1
464	
465	            # Fail-safe budget escalation.
466	            if attempts_on_tier > cfg.tier_attempt_budget and tier_idx + 1 < tier_count:
467	                tier_idx += 1
468	                _log.warning("tier budget exhausted -> escalate to %s (fail-safe)",
469	                             self.tiers[tier_idx].name)
470	                drift_count, prev_class, attempts_on_tier = 0, "", 1
471	
472	            tier = self.tiers[tier_idx]
473	            err_text = result.log_text
474	            cur_progress = result.depth()
475	            prior_class = classify_error(err_text)
476	            _log.info("attempt %d/%d %s tier=%s (%d/%d) prior=%s progress=%d",
477	                      attempt, max_attempts, self.phase_name, tier.name,
478	                      attempts_on_tier, cfg.tier_attempt_budget, prior_class, cur_progress)
479	
480	            lessons = self.lessons.format_for_prompt(self.phase_name)
481	            playbook = self._trajectory_playbook(prior_class)
482	            known_fixes = self._replay_reference(err_text)
483	            prompt = build_fix_prompt(
484	                self.phase_name, err_text, lessons=lessons, attempt=attempt,
485	                prior_class=prior_class, user_context=cfg.user_context,
486	                skill_playbook=load_fix_playbook(),
487	                trajectories=playbook, known_fixes=known_fixes,
488	                prior_diff=prior.diff if prior else "",
489	                prior_state=self._format_prior_state(prior),
490	            )
491	            (self.fix_log_dir / f"prompt_{attempt}.txt").write_text(prompt)
492	
493	            agent_log = self.fix_log_dir / f"attempt_{attempt}.log"
494	            outcome = _coerce_outcome(
495	                self.run_agent(tier, prompt, agent_log, self.session_id))
496	            output = outcome.text
497	            if outcome.timed_out:
498	                _log.warning("attempt %d timed out (rc=%d); edits may be partial -- "
499	                             "surfacing to next attempt as prior-state", attempt, outcome.rc)
500	            self._accrue_tokens(output)
501	            analysis = AgentAnalysis.parse(output)
502	            self._trail_append(rejected_trail, analysis)
503	            # Snapshot this attempt for the NEXT one. On the punt/escalate paths below
504	            # `result` is still the pre-attempt failure (correct: nothing was fixed);
505	            # the re-run paths refresh it and re-snapshot before looping.
506	            prior = self._make_prior(attempt, outcome, analysis, result)
507	
508	            # UNFIXABLE: escalate if possible, else abort.
509	            if analysis.verdict is Verdict.UNFIXABLE:
510	                reason = analysis.unfixable_reason or "declared UNFIXABLE"
511	                if tier_idx + 1 < tier_count:
512	                    tier_idx += 1
513	                    _log.warning("UNFIXABLE (%s) -> escalate to %s", reason,
514	                                 self.tiers[tier_idx].name)
515	                    drift_count, prev_class, attempts_on_tier = 0, "", 0
516	                    continue
517	                _log.warning("UNFIXABLE (%s), no stronger tier; aborting", reason)
518	                self._save(err_text, "unfixable", f"UNFIXABLE: {reason}", analysis)
519	                self._log_stat("unresolved", error_class=self._effective_class(analysis, err_text),
520	                               tier=tier.name)
521	                return FixResult(ok=False, attempts=attempt, tier_index=tier_idx,
522	                                 reason=f"unfixable: {reason}", final_analysis=analysis)
523	
524	            # ESCALATE request.
525	            if analysis.verdict is Verdict.ESCALATE and tier_idx + 1 < tier_count:
526	                tier_idx += 1
527	                _log.warning("agent requested ESCALATE -> %s", self.tiers[tier_idx].name)
528	                drift_count, prev_class, attempts_on_tier = 0, "", 0
529	                continue
530	
531	            # Drift / progress detection.
532	            eff_class = self._effective_class(analysis, err_text)
533	            if cur_progress > max_progress:
534	                if drift_count > 0:
535	                    _log.info("progress to layer %d -> reset drift", cur_progress)
536	                drift_count = 0
537	            elif attempt > 1:
538	                same = self._same_error(eff_class, prev_class, err_text, prev_text)
539	                if same is True:
540	                    drift_count += 1
541	                    _log.warning("same error '%s' streak=%d/%d",
542	                                 eff_class, drift_count, cfg.drift_threshold)
543	                    if drift_count >= cfg.drift_threshold:
544	                        if tier_idx + 1 < tier_count:
545	                            tier_idx += 1
546	                            _log.warning("drift on '%s' -> escalate to %s",
547	                                         eff_class, self.tiers[tier_idx].name)
548	                            drift_count, prev_class, attempts_on_tier = 0, "", 0
549	                            prev_text = err_text
550	                            continue
551	                        _log.warning("drift on '%s', no stronger tier; aborting", eff_class)
552	                        self._save(err_text, "drift",
553	                                   f"Stuck on '{eff_class}' for {drift_count} attempts",
554	                                   analysis)
555	                        self._log_stat("unresolved", error_class=eff_class, tier=tier.name)
556	                        return FixResult(ok=False, attempts=attempt, tier_index=tier_idx,
557	                                         reason=f"drift: {eff_class}", final_analysis=analysis)
558	                elif same is False:
559	                    if drift_count > 0:
560	                        _log.info("error changed '%s'->'%s' (progress)", prev_class, eff_class)
561	                    drift_count = 0
562	                # same is None -> fail-safe: keep trying, no reset
563	
564	            if eff_class and eff_class != "unknown":
565	                prev_class = eff_class
566	            prev_text = err_text
567	            max_progress = max(max_progress, cur_progress)
568	
569	            # CUDA guard: a fix must not silently drop us to CPU.
570	            if cuda_was_available and self.cuda_guard and not self.cuda_guard():
571	                _log.error("CUDA became unavailable after fix (attempt %d); refusing CPU re-run",
572	                           attempt)
573	                with agent_log.open("a") as fh:
574	                    fh.write("\n[harness] REGRESSION: torch.cuda.is_available()==False after "
575	                             "your fix. Restore the matching CUDA torch wheel and verify before "
576	                             "anything else.\n")
577	                self._save(err_text, "still_failing",
578	                           f"Fix broke CUDA (attempt {attempt}); refused CPU re-run", analysis)
579	                result = PhaseResult(ok=False, log_text=agent_log.read_text())
580	                prior = self._make_prior(attempt, outcome, analysis, result)
581	                continue
582	
583	            # Re-run the phase to verify the fix.
584	            _log.info("re-running %s after fix (attempt %d)", self.phase_name, attempt)
585	            result = self.run_phase()
586	            if result.ok:
587	                note = analysis.fix_plan or analysis.root_cause or f"fixed on attempt {attempt}"
588	                self._save(err_text, "fixed", note[:500], analysis)
589	                self._record_patch(err_text)
590	                self._record_trajectory(err_text, analysis, rejected_trail,
591	                                        tier=tier.name, steps=attempt)
592	                # Under reference-only replay a matching recorded fix is never
593	                # auto-applied, so a success while `known_fixes` was injected means
594	                # the agent consulted+adopted recorded knowledge -> credit it.
595	                fix_outcome = "reference_used" if known_fixes else "agent_fixed"
596	                self._log_stat(fix_outcome, error_class=self._effective_class(analysis, err_text),
597	                               tier=tier.name)
598	                _log.info("phase %s fixed on attempt %d (tier %s)",
599	                          self.phase_name, attempt, tier.name)
600	                return FixResult(ok=True, attempts=attempt, tier_index=tier_idx,
601	                                 final_analysis=analysis)
602	
603	            self._save(err_text, "still_failing",
604	                       f"Attempt {attempt} did not resolve", analysis)
605	            # Refresh prior-state with the authoritative re-run outcome for the next attempt.
606	            prior = self._make_prior(attempt, outcome, analysis, result)
607	
608	        _log.error("%s failed after %d fix attempts", self.phase_name, max_attempts)
609	        self._log_stat("unresolved", error_class=prev_class)
610	        return FixResult(ok=False, attempts=attempt, tier_index=tier_idx,
611	                         reason="max_attempts_exhausted")
612	
613	
614	def run_fix_loop(
615	    phase_name: str,
616	    run_phase: PhaseRunner,
617	    *,
618	    config: FixLoopConfig | None = None,
619	    out_dir: Path | None = None,
620	    run_agent: AgentRunner | None = None,
621	    lesson_store: LessonStore | None = None,
622	    model_id: str = "unknown",
623	    scheme: str = "",

634	        lesson_store=lesson_store, model_id=model_id, scheme=scheme, method=method,

1	"""Tier ladder: map tier names to an agent backend + model + env overrides.
2	
3	Ports ``agent_tier_activate`` from ``local_dispatch/agent/agent_backends.sh``.  A
4	tier is a named rung on the escalation ladder (cheapest first).  Resolving a tier
5	yields the backend to invoke, the wire model, and any extra environment the
6	backend process needs (e.g. Copilot BYOK provider settings for MiniMax).
7	
8	Secrets are never embedded here -- only the *names* of env vars the backend reads
9	(``MINIMAX_API_KEY``, ``COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN``) are referenced at run time.
10	"""
11	
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
15	
16	
17	@dataclass(frozen=True)
18	class Tier:
19	    name: str
20	    backend: str                       # "openclaw" | "copilot"
21	    model: str | None = None           # wire model name (None => backend default)
22	    env: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # extra env for the backend
23	    byok: bool = False                 # Copilot BYOK (custom provider, no GitHub auth)
24	
25	    def describe(self) -> str:
26	        return f"{self.name}(backend={self.backend}, model={self.model or 'default'})"
27	
28	
29	# MiniMax BYOK defaults (Copilot driving a non-GitHub model via its own provider).
30	_MINIMAX_BYOK_ENV = {
31	    "COPILOT_MINIMAX": "1",
32	    "COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL": "https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic",
33	    "COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE": "anthropic",
34	    "COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID": "claude-sonnet-4",
35	}
36	
37	
38	def resolve_tier(name: str) -> Tier:
39	    """Map a tier name to a concrete :class:`Tier` (unknown => copilot + that model)."""
40	    key = name.strip().lower()
41	    if key == "openclaw":
42	        return Tier(name="openclaw", backend="openclaw")
43	    if key == "minimax":
44	        # Copilot BYOK against MiniMax-M3, reusing MINIMAX_API_KEY (no GitHub auth).
45	        return Tier(name="minimax", backend="copilot", model="MiniMax-M3",
46	                    env=dict(_MINIMAX_BYOK_ENV), byok=True)
47	    if key == "opus":
48	        return Tier(name="opus", backend="copilot", model="claude-opus-4.8")
49	    if key == "sonnet":
50	        return Tier(name="sonnet", backend="copilot", model="claude-sonnet-4.5")
51	    if key == "copilot":
52	        return Tier(name="copilot", backend="copilot")
53	    # Unknown name => copilot backend with that string as the model override.
54	    return Tier(name=key, backend="copilot", model=name)
55	
56	
57	def resolve_tiers(names: list[str]) -> list[Tier]:
58	    """Resolve an ordered ladder of tier names; empty => the default two-tier ladder."""
59	    if not names:
60	        names = ["openclaw", "minimax"]
61	    return [resolve_tier(n) for n in names]

1	"""Build the structured fix-attempt prompt for the agent.
2	
3	Ports ``build_fix_prompt`` from ``local_dispatch/agent/agent_fix_loop.sh``.  The
4	prompt asks the agent to emit a strict, machine-parseable analysis block first
5	(COMPONENT / ERROR_CLASS / ... / VERDICT / SMOKE_TEST) -- this is what
6	:mod:`aqa.agent.verdict` parses to drive the escalation/drift state machine.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	from pathlib import Path
12	
13	_FIX_PLAYBOOK_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "recipes" / "fix_playbook.md"
14	
15	
16	def load_fix_playbook() -> str:
17	    """Return the packaged fix-agent troubleshooting playbook (best-effort).
18	
19	    This is durable, cross-run domain knowledge embedded into every fix prompt as
20	    REFERENCE. A missing/unreadable asset degrades gracefully to an empty string.
21	    Per-run, box/model-specific guidance should go through ``agent.context`` instead.
22	    """
23	    try:
24	        return _FIX_PLAYBOOK_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
25	    except OSError:
26	        return ""
27	
28	
29	_PROTOCOL = """\
30	You MUST print the block below FIRST, before changing any code or installing anything.
31	Do NOT modify code until you have printed an EVIDENCE_RESULT from a READ-ONLY command
32	that supports your hypothesis. No guessing.
33	
34	COMPONENT: <our_code|transformers|auto_round|vllm|vllm_omni|diffusers|torch|model_code|data|environment>
35	ERROR_CLASS: <ONE stable snake_case token naming THIS error's category. Reuse the same
36	             token every time the same underlying error recurs (drives drift detection).>
37	ROOT_CAUSE_HYPOTHESIS: <one falsifiable sentence -- the specific cause>
38	EVIDENCE_CMD: <a single read-only command that verifies the hypothesis>
39	EVIDENCE_RESULT: <paste the command's output>
40	VERDICT: <FIXABLE | UNFIXABLE | ESCALATE>
41	UNFIXABLE_REASON: <required only if UNFIXABLE>
42	FIX_TIER: <config | upgrade | workaround | patch>   # always try the LOWEST that works
43	FIX_PLAN: <3 lines max -- what you will change and why it fixes the ROOT CAUSE>
44	SMOKE_TEST: <ONE fast, MECHANISM-LEVEL command that proves the FIX MECHANISM holds.
45	             Target ~30s. It must NOT be the full phase: do NOT run full lm_eval, do NOT
46	             boot the whole vLLM engine / load the whole model, do NOT re-quantize end to
47	             end -- the harness re-runs the FULL phase itself to verify, so duplicating it
48	             only burns your time budget. Instead verify the SPECIFIC thing your fix
49	             changed, e.g.: `python -c "import <edited_module>"` or `python -m py_compile
50	             <edited_file>` (edit didn't break imports/syntax); read the checkpoint's
51	             quantization config JSON and assert the offending layer is now in the
52	             ignore-list; read a safetensors HEADER (not a full load) and assert an edited
53	             weight's dtype; or import JUST the failing kernel/layer and call it once on a
54	             tiny dummy tensor of the offending shape to reproduce (or clear) the exact
55	             assertion. Prefer the cheapest check that exercises the SAME mechanism the
56	             error came from.>
57	
58	## Rules
59	- If VERDICT is UNFIXABLE: print the block and STOP (no wasted retries).
60	- If the fix needs a MORE CAPABLE model (deep multi-file reasoning, subtle mixed-precision
61	  layout, hard custom-model patch), set VERDICT: ESCALATE and STOP with a clear reason.
62	- Prefer the LOWEST FIX_TIER; patching source is a last resort.
63	- After applying the fix, RUN your MECHANISM-LEVEL SMOKE_TEST yourself and show its output
64	  before finishing. Iterate on cheap checks as much as you need -- but never use the full
65	  phase (full lm_eval / whole-engine boot / full re-quantize) as your smoke; the harness
66	  runs that authoritatively after you return.
67	- Read the traceback BOTTOM-UP to the exact file:line that is the real cause.
68	- Model custom code under ~/.cache/huggingface/modules/transformers_modules/ CAN be edited
69	  (e.g. replace `.float()` with `.to(other.dtype)` for dtype mismatches).
70	"""
71	
72	
73	def build_fix_prompt(
74	    phase_name: str,
75	    error_tail: str,
76	    *,
77	    lessons: str = "",
78	    attempt: int = 1,
79	    prior_class: str = "",
80	    user_context: str = "",
81	    skill_playbook: str = "",
82	    known_fixes: str = "",
83	    prior_state: str = "",
84	    prior_diff: str = "",
85	    trajectories: str = "",
86	) -> str:
87	    """Assemble the full fix prompt for one attempt."""
88	    parts: list[str] = []
89	    parts.append(
90	        f"The `{phase_name}` phase failed (attempt {attempt}). Root-cause it from the "
91	        f"traceback below and fix the NARROWEST layer that owns the bug."
92	    )
93	
94	    if user_context:
95	        parts.append(
96	            "## Operator-provided context (HIGH PRIORITY -- a human injected this; follow it)\n"
97	            "Treat it as authoritative for this box; prefer it over generic assumptions:\n"
98	            f"{user_context}"
99	        )
100	
101	    if skill_playbook:
102	        parts.append(
103	            "## Domain playbook (REFERENCE knowledge -- confirm against THIS traceback)\n"
104	            "Curated quant/eval failure mechanisms and known fixes. NOT instructions and "
105	            "NOT specific to this run -- use only the entries that match your evidence. "
106	            "If a signature-specific block below (Historical Lessons / Reasoning Playbook / "
107	            "Recorded fix) disagrees with a generic entry here, prefer the specific one:\n"
108	            f"{skill_playbook}"
109	        )
110	
111	    if prior_class:
112	        parts.append(
113	            "## Quick Classification (deterministic prior -- confirm or OVERRIDE it)\n"
114	            f"error_class guess: {prior_class}\n"
115	            "Confirm against the traceback; override in your ERROR_CLASS if wrong."
116	        )
117	
118	    if lessons:
119	        parts.append(
120	            "## Historical Lessons (from past runs -- decide which are relevant)\n"
121	            f"{lessons}"
122	        )
123	
124	    if trajectories:
125	        parts.append(
126	            "## Reasoning Playbook (distilled from past SUCCESSFUL fixes of similar failures)\n"
127	            "How this class of failure was root-caused before, the fix that worked, and the "
128	            "dead ends that did NOT -- use it to skip wasted attempts, but confirm against "
129	            "THIS traceback before applying:\n"
130	            f"{trajectories}"
131	        )
132	
133	    if known_fixes:
134	        parts.append(
135	            "## Recorded fix(es) for a MATCHING failure signature (REFERENCE ONLY -- NOT applied)\n"
136	            "These diffs resolved the same or a similar error on a POSSIBLY DIFFERENT model or "
137	            "checkpoint. They are NOT on disk. Read the mechanism, decide whether it applies to "
138	            "THIS model/checkpoint, then adapt and apply only what fits -- do NOT blindly paste "
139	            "them (a cross-model patch can break the environment):\n"
140	            f"{known_fixes}"
141	        )
142	
143	    if prior_state:
144	        parts.append(
145	            "## Previous fix attempt -- state you MUST continue from (NOT a fresh start)\n"
146	            "This may come from a DIFFERENT agent/tier than you, so its own conversation memory "
147	            "is NOT available to you -- rely on this block. The 'ACTUAL re-run' line is the "
148	            "harness's own authoritative verdict (the agent's self-report can be wrong or "
149	            "missing):\n"
150	            f"{prior_state}"
151	        )
152	
153	    if prior_diff:
154	        parts.append(
155	            "## Changes ALREADY made by earlier fix tiers (consolidate, don't restart)\n"
156	            "You are the STRONGEST tier and the patch CONSOLIDATOR. This unified diff is on "
157	            "disk now; keep what helps, fix what is wrong or incomplete:\n"
158	            f"```diff\n{prior_diff}\n```"
159	        )
160	
161	    parts.append(f"## Error output (tail)\n```\n{error_tail}\n```")
162	    parts.append(_PROTOCOL)
163	    return "\n\n".join(parts)

1	"""Eval-aware self-heal -- the "agent-as-operator" layer for the eval RUN itself.
2	
3	The generic agent fix-loop (:mod:`aqa.agent.fix_loop`) can already drive a failing
4	``evaluate`` phase to success by editing the working tree. But many eval failures
5	are *operational* and don't need an LLM at all: an OOM just needs a smaller batch,
6	a flaky endpoint just needs a retry, an all-zero instruct run usually needs the
7	chat template toggled. Spending an agent tier (minutes + tokens) on those is waste.
8	
9	This module adds a cheap **deterministic pre-pass**: classify the eval failure and
10	apply a targeted config quick-fix, retrying without the agent. Only failures that
11	resist the quick-fixes escalate to the agent -- and when they do, we hand the agent
12	an eval-specific hint so it fixes the *eval env/config*, not quantization. This is
13	the differentiator over launcher-style tools (NEL): the eval run heals itself.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	import re
19	import time
20	from collections.abc import Callable
21	from dataclasses import dataclass
22	
23	from ..config import EvalConfig
24	from ..logging_util import get_logger
25	
26	_log = get_logger("eval.heal")
27	
28	# Ordered (class, pattern) -- first match wins. Eval-specific, distinct from the
29	# quant-oriented drift classifier.
30	_EVAL_RULES: list[tuple[str, re.Pattern[str]]] = [
31	    ("oom", re.compile(
32	        r"CUDA out of memory|OutOfMemoryError|torch\.cuda\.OutOfMemory|"
33	        r"No available memory for the cache|KV cache .* (?:memory|blocks)|"

127	class EvalHealer:
128	    """Owns the (mutable) eval config and proposes deterministic quick-fixes.
129	
130	    ``propose(log)`` classifies the failure, mutates ``cfg`` in place when a cheap
131	    remedy exists, and returns the applied :class:`QuickFix` (or ``None`` when no
132	    deterministic fix applies or the ladder is exhausted -- signalling "escalate").
133	    Because the pipeline's eval phase reads the *same* ``cfg`` object, mutations
134	    take effect on the next re-run.
135	    """
136	
137	    def __init__(
138	        self,
139	        cfg: EvalConfig,
140	        *,
141	        max_transient_retries: int = 2,
142	        backoff_s: float = 5.0,
143	        sleep: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep,
144	    ):
145	        self.cfg = cfg
146	        self.applied: list[str] = []
147	        self.last_failure = ""
148	        self._transient = 0
149	        self._max_transient = max_transient_retries
150	        self._backoff = backoff_s
151	        self._sleep = sleep
152	
153	    def propose(self, log_text: str) -> QuickFix | None:
154	        cls = classify_eval_failure(log_text)
155	        self.last_failure = cls
156	        if cls == "oom":
157	            return self._fix_oom()
158	        if cls in ("endpoint", "engine_crash"):
159	            return self._fix_transient(cls)
160	        if cls in ("chat_template", "empty_output"):
161	            return self._fix_chat_template(cls)
162	        return None
163	
164	    # -- individual remedies ------------------------------------------------
165	    def _fix_oom(self) -> QuickFix | None:
166	        cur = str(self.cfg.batch_size)
167	        idx = _BATCH_LADDER.index(cur) if cur in _BATCH_LADDER else 0
168	        if idx + 1 < len(_BATCH_LADDER):
169	            new = _BATCH_LADDER[idx + 1]
170	            self.cfg.batch_size = new
171	            self.applied.append(f"batch_size={new}")
172	            return QuickFix("oom", f"OOM: shrink batch_size {cur} -> {new}")
173	        # batch already minimal -> lower vllm gpu_memory_utilization.
174	        args = self.cfg.lm_eval.model_args
175	        cur_mem = float(args.get("gpu_memory_utilization", _MEM_LADDER[0]))
176	        below = [m for m in _MEM_LADDER if m < cur_mem]
177	        if below:
178	            new_mem = below[0]
179	            args["gpu_memory_utilization"] = new_mem
180	            self.applied.append(f"gpu_memory_utilization={new_mem}")
181	            return QuickFix("oom", f"OOM: lower gpu_memory_utilization {cur_mem} -> {new_mem}")
182	        return None
183	
184	    def _fix_transient(self, cls: str) -> QuickFix | None:
185	        if self._transient >= self._max_transient:
186	            return None
187	        self._transient += 1
188	        wait = self._backoff * self._transient
189	        _log.info("transient %s failure -> retry %d/%d after %.0fs",
190	                  cls, self._transient, self._max_transient, wait)
191	        self._sleep(wait)
192	        return QuickFix(cls, f"{cls}: transient, retry {self._transient}/{self._max_transient}",
193	                        transient=True)
194	
195	    def _fix_chat_template(self, cls: str) -> QuickFix | None:
196	        if "chat_template_toggled" in self.applied:
197	            return None
198	        current = self.cfg.lm_eval.apply_chat_template
199	        new = not current if current is not None else True
200	        self.cfg.lm_eval.apply_chat_template = new
201	        self.applied.append("chat_template_toggled")
202	        return QuickFix(cls, f"{cls}: toggle apply_chat_template {current} -> {new}")

1	"""lm-evaluation-harness adapter.
2	
3	Builds and runs the exact ``lm_eval`` invocation the historic
4	``local_dispatch/phases/evaluate.sh`` used, then parses lm-eval's own results
5	json.  Generative tasks (chat-template + fewshot-as-multiturn + generation
6	budget) vs loglikelihood tasks are handled per the recipe's ``type``.
7	"""

22	# traceback (not just the "rc=1" wrapper) reaches the fix-loop's error signature.

26	def _log_tail(path: Path, lines: int = _FAIL_TAIL_LINES) -> str:
27	    """Return the tail of an lm_eval run log, prefixed for readability.
28	
29	    The exception the harness raises otherwise carries only a generic
30	    ``lm_eval failed for … (rc=1)`` wrapper; embedding the log tail lets
31	    ``extract_signature``/``classify_error`` key knowledge on the *actual*
32	    error (e.g. an ``AssertionError`` from a kernel) instead of the task list.
33	    """
34	    try:
35	        text = path.read_text(errors="replace")
36	    except OSError:
37	        return ""

39	    return f"\n--- {path.name} (last {lines} lines) ---\n{tail}" if tail else ""

42	class LmEvalHarness:

44	
45	    def __init__(
46	        self,
47	        *,
48	        num_gpus: int = 1,
49	        batch_size: str = "auto",
50	        limit: int | None = None,

65	        self.apply_chat_template = apply_chat_template

70	
71	    def _is_generative(self, recipe: BenchmarkRecipe) -> bool:
72	        if self.apply_chat_template is not None:
73	            return recipe.type == "generative" or self.apply_chat_template
74	        return recipe.type == "generative" or recipe.apply_chat_template
