153	    # -- HF sync ---------------------------------------------------------
154	    def sync_down(self) -> bool:
155	        """Pull the knowledge subtree from the HF dataset into the local dir.
156	
157	        No-op (returns False) without a ``repo``; best-effort otherwise -- an
158	        offline host or a fresh/empty repo simply leaves the local cache as-is.
159	        """
160	        if not self.repo:
161	            return False
162	        token = resolve_hf_token(None, self.token_env)
163	        try:
164	            from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
165	        except ImportError:
166	            _log.info("knowledge: huggingface_hub not installed; local-only mode")
167	            return False
168	        try:
169	            snap = snapshot_download(
170	                repo_id=self.repo, repo_type="dataset", token=token,
171	                endpoint=self.endpoint, allow_patterns=[f"{self.path_in_repo}/**"],
172	            )
173	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - offline / empty repo / auth: soft-fail
174	            _log.info("knowledge: sync_down skipped (%s)", exc)
175	            return False
176	        src = Path(snap) / self.path_in_repo
177	        if not src.is_dir():
178	            return False
179	        merged = self._merge_tree(src, self.local_dir)
180	        _log.info("knowledge: synced down from %s (%d file(s))", self.repo, merged)
181	        return True
182	
183	    def _merge_tree(self, src: Path, dst: Path) -> int:
184	        """Copy ``src`` into ``dst``; lessons JSONL is merged (dedup by signature)."""
185	        count = 0
186	        for p in src.rglob("*"):
187	            if not p.is_file():
188	                continue
189	            rel = p.relative_to(src)
190	            target = dst / rel
191	            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
192	            if (rel.parts and rel.parts[0] in ("lessons", "trajectories")
193	                    and target.exists()):
194	                self._merge_lessons(target, p)
195	            else:
196	                shutil.copy2(p, target)
197	            count += 1
198	        return count
199	
200	    @staticmethod
201	    def _merge_lessons(local: Path, remote: Path) -> None:
202	        by_sig: dict[str, dict] = {}
203	        for src in (local, remote):  # remote wins on conflict (freshest shared truth)
204	            for line in src.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
205	                line = line.strip()
206	                if not line:
207	                    continue
208	                try:
209	                    obj = json.loads(line)
210	                except json.JSONDecodeError:
211	                    continue
212	                by_sig[obj.get("signature", line)] = obj
213	        local.write_text(
214	            "\n".join(json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False) for v in by_sig.values()) + "\n"
215	        )
216	
217	    def push_up(self) -> bool:
218	        """Upload the local knowledge dir back to the HF dataset (best-effort)."""
219	        if not self.repo or not self.push:
220	            return False
221	        token = resolve_hf_token(None, self.token_env)
222	        if not token:
223	            _log.info("knowledge: no write token; not pushing to %s", self.repo)
224	            return False
225	        try:
226	            from huggingface_hub import HfApi
227	        except ImportError:
228	            return False
229	        try:
230	            api = HfApi(token=token, endpoint=self.endpoint)
231	            api.upload_folder(
232	                repo_id=self.repo, repo_type="dataset", folder_path=str(self.local_dir),
233	                path_in_repo=self.path_in_repo, token=token,
234	                commit_message="aqa: update shared fix-knowledge",
235	            )
236	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - never fail a run on a knowledge push
237	            _log.warning("knowledge: push_up to %s failed: %s", self.repo, exc)
238	            return False
239	        _log.info("knowledge: pushed lessons/patches to %s", self.repo)
240	        return True
241	
242	    # -- patch archive ---------------------------------------------------
243	    def _patch_root(self, phase: str) -> Path:
244	        return self.local_dir / "patches" / phase
245	
246	    def find_patches(self, phase: str, error_text: str,
247	                     error_class: str = "") -> list[PatchRecord]:
248	        """Recorded patches for this failure, best-match first.
249	
250	        Ranking tiers (finest first): exact signature > exact exception class +
251	        semantic category > exact exception class > semantic category > other.
252	        Newest ``ts`` breaks ties within a tier. Cross-model by design -- the key
253	        is the error, not the model. ``patch --dry-run`` is the real safety net,
254	        so a looser tier only ever affects *which candidate is tried first*.
255	        """
256	        root = self._patch_root(phase)
257	        if not root.is_dir():
258	            return []
259	        signature = extract_signature(error_text)
260	        want_class = error_class or classify_error(error_text)
261	        want_exc = exception_type(error_text)
262	        records: list[PatchRecord] = []
263	        for meta_path in root.glob("*/meta.json"):
264	            try:
265	                meta = json.loads(meta_path.read_text())
266	            except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
267	                continue
268	            patch_files = {
269	                p.stem: p for p in meta_path.parent.glob("*.patch") if p.stem != "combined"
270	            }
271	            if not patch_files:
272	                continue
273	            records.append(PatchRecord(
274	                phase=phase, sig_hash=meta_path.parent.name,
275	                signature=meta.get("signature", ""), error_class=meta.get("error_class", ""),
276	                patch_files=patch_files, exc_type=meta.get("exc_type", ""),
277	                model_id=meta.get("model_id", ""),
278	                scheme=meta.get("scheme", ""), method=meta.get("method", ""),
279	                ts=meta.get("ts", ""),
280	            ))
281	
282	        def rank(r: PatchRecord) -> int:
283	            if r.signature and r.signature == signature:
284	                return 0
285	            exc_ok = bool(want_exc) and r.exc_type == want_exc
286	            cls_ok = want_class not in ("", "unknown") and r.error_class == want_class
287	            if exc_ok and cls_ok:
288	                return 1
289	            if exc_ok:
290	                return 2
291	            if cls_ok:
292	                return 3
293	            return 4
294	
295	        # Newest-first within each match tier: sort by ts desc, then stably by tier.
296	        records.sort(key=lambda r: r.ts, reverse=True)
297	        records.sort(key=rank)
298	        return records
299	
300	    def record(self, phase: str, error_text: str, patch_files: dict[str, Path], *,
301	               error_class: str = "", model_id: str = "", scheme: str = "",
302	               method: str = "") -> PatchRecord | None:
303	        """Archive a successful fix's patches keyed by the error signature.
304	
305	        ``patch_files`` is the ``{label: path}`` map from
306	        :meth:`PatchCapture.write_patches` (the ``combined`` entry is ignored).
307	        Returns the stored record, or None if there were no per-area patches.
308	        """
309	        per_area = {k: v for k, v in patch_files.items() if k != "combined"}
310	        if not per_area:
311	            return None
312	        signature = extract_signature(error_text)
313	        err_class = error_class or classify_error(error_text)
314	        exc = exception_type(error_text)
315	        sig_hash = signature_hash(signature)
316	        dest = self._patch_root(phase) / sig_hash
317	        dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
318	        stored: dict[str, Path] = {}
319	        for label, src in per_area.items():
320	            src = Path(src)
321	            if not src.is_file():
322	                continue
323	            out = dest / f"{label}.patch"
324	            shutil.copy2(src, out)
325	            stored[label] = out
326	        if not stored:
327	            return None
328	        ts = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())
329	        (dest / "meta.json").write_text(json.dumps({
330	            "signature": signature, "error_class": err_class, "exc_type": exc,
331	            "model_id": model_id, "scheme": scheme, "method": method, "ts": ts,
332	        }, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
333	        _log.info("knowledge: recorded patch for '%s'/%s (%s) -> %s",
334	                  err_class, exc or "-", signature[:60], sig_hash)
335	        return PatchRecord(
336	            phase=phase, sig_hash=sig_hash, signature=signature, error_class=err_class,
337	            patch_files=stored, exc_type=exc, model_id=model_id, scheme=scheme,
338	            method=method, ts=ts,
339	        )
340	
341	    # -- replay statistics (埋点) -----------------------------------------
342	    _STAT_OUTCOMES = ("replay_hit", "reference_used", "agent_fixed", "unresolved")
343	
344	    def record_trajectory(self, summary: TrajectorySummary) -> dict | None:
345	        """Persist one distilled fix-trajectory summary (best-effort).
346	
347	        Complements :meth:`record` (the replayable patch) with the *reasoning*
348	        behind it, keyed by the same signature. Never raises -- knowledge
349	        capture must not fail a run.
350	        """
351	        try:
352	            return self.trajectories.save(summary.phase, summary)
353	        except OSError as exc:
354	            _log.warning("knowledge: could not record trajectory: %s", exc)
355	            return None
356	
357	    def _stats_path(self) -> Path:
358	        return self.local_dir / "stats" / "events.jsonl"
359	
360	    def log_event(self, phase: str, outcome: str, *, sig_hash: str = "",
361	                  error_class: str = "", model_id: str = "", tier: str = "") -> None:
362	        """Append one replay/heal outcome event (best-effort telemetry).
363	
364	        ``outcome`` is one of :data:`_STAT_OUTCOMES`: ``replay_hit`` (a recorded
365	        patch resolved the failure with no agent call -- legacy, auto-apply is
366	        disabled under reference-only replay so this stays 0), ``reference_used``
367	        (an agent tier resolved it *while* a matching recorded fix was injected as
368	        reference, i.e. knowledge demonstrably contributed), ``agent_fixed`` (an
369	        agent tier resolved it with no matching recorded fix available), or
370	        ``unresolved`` (gave up). Drives the hit-rate metric.
371	        """
372	        path = self._stats_path()
373	        try:
374	            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
375	            row = {
376	                "ts": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
377	                "phase": phase, "outcome": outcome, "sig_hash": sig_hash,
378	                "error_class": error_class, "model_id": model_id, "tier": tier,
379	            }
380	            with path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
381	                fh.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
382	        except OSError as exc:
383	            _log.warning("knowledge: could not log stat event: %s", exc)
384	
385	    def stats(self) -> dict:
386	        """Aggregate replay telemetry: counts per outcome + knowledge hit-rate.
387	
388	        ``hit_rate`` = (replay_hit + reference_used) / (all outcomes), i.e. the
389	        fraction of *fixable* failures where recorded knowledge demonstrably
390	        contributed -- either auto-applied (``replay_hit``, legacy/0 under
391	        reference-only replay) or consulted-and-adopted by the agent
392	        (``reference_used``). ``agent_fixed`` counts fixes the agent found with no
393	        matching recorded knowledge available.
394	        """
395	        counts = dict.fromkeys(self._STAT_OUTCOMES, 0)
396	        path = self._stats_path()
397	        if path.is_file():
398	            for line in path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
399	                line = line.strip()
400	                if not line:
401	                    continue
402	                try:
403	                    outcome = json.loads(line).get("outcome", "")
404	                except json.JSONDecodeError:
405	                    continue
406	                if outcome in counts:
407	                    counts[outcome] += 1
408	        total = sum(counts.values())
409	        counts["total"] = total
410	        knowledge_hits = counts["replay_hit"] + counts["reference_used"]
411	        counts["hit_rate"] = round(knowledge_hits / total, 4) if total else 0.0
412	        counts["trajectories"] = self._count_trajectories()
413	        return counts
414	
415	    def _count_trajectories(self) -> int:
416	        """Total distilled trajectory summaries stored across all phases."""
417	        root = self.local_dir / "trajectories"
418	        if not root.is_dir():
419	            return 0
420	        n = 0
421	        for p in root.glob("*.jsonl"):
422	            for line in p.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
423	                if line.strip():
424	                    n += 1
425	        return n

1	"""Provision the agent-fix backends' config into the runtime home directory.
2	
3	Ports the ``~/.openclaw`` / ``~/.copilot`` setup that
4	``local_dispatch/remote_exec.py`` does inside the container so the fix-loop's
5	OpenClaw and Copilot backends are authenticated and skill-aware by default.
6	
7	What it lays down (idempotent):
8	  * ``~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`` + ``~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/auth-profiles.json``
9	    from the bundled templates, with ``MINIMAX_API_KEY`` synced into the MiniMax
10	    auth profiles (openclaw's tier-0 provider).
11	  * ``~/.copilot/settings.json`` from the bundled template (model/effort defaults).
12	  * The project skills copied into ``~/.copilot/skills`` and
13	    ``~/.openclaw/workspace/skills`` so both backends share the same recipe
14	    knowledge (single source of truth).
15	
16	Secrets are read from the environment only (``--minimax-env`` names the var);
17	nothing is inlined. Run as ``python -m aqa.agent.provision`` inside the container.
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	import argparse
23	import json
24	import os
25	import shutil
26	from pathlib import Path
27	
28	from ..logging_util import get_logger
29	
30	_log = get_logger("agent.provision")
31	
32	_ASSETS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "assets"
33	_MINIMAX_PROFILES = ("minimax-global", "minimax:cn", "minimax:global")
34	
35	
36	def _copy_tree(src: Path, dst: Path) -> None:
37	    """Overlay ``src`` contents onto ``dst`` (like ``cp -a src/. dst/``)."""
38	    dst.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
39	    for item in src.iterdir():
40	        target = dst / item.name
41	        if item.is_dir():
42	            _copy_tree(item, target)
43	        else:
44	            shutil.copy2(item, target)
45	
46	
47	def sync_minimax_key(auth_path: Path, key: str) -> bool:
48	    """Write ``key`` into the MiniMax profiles of an openclaw auth-profiles file."""
49	    try:
50	        data = json.loads(auth_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
51	    except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
52	        _log.warning("cannot sync MiniMax key into %s: %s", auth_path, exc)
53	        return False
54	    profiles = data.setdefault("profiles", {})
55	    updated = False
56	    for name in _MINIMAX_PROFILES:
57	        prof = profiles.get(name)
58	        if isinstance(prof, dict) and prof.get("provider") == "minimax":
59	            prof["key"] = key
60	            updated = True
61	    if updated:
62	        auth_path.write_text(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n",
63	                             encoding="utf-8")
64	    return updated
65	
66	
67	def provision_openclaw(home: Path, minimax_key: str | None) -> None:
68	    src = _ASSETS / "openclaw"
69	    if not src.is_dir():
70	        _log.warning("bundled openclaw assets missing at %s", src)
71	        return
72	    dst = home / ".openclaw"
73	    _copy_tree(src, dst)
74	    if minimax_key:
75	        auth = dst / "agents" / "main" / "agent" / "auth-profiles.json"
76	        if sync_minimax_key(auth, minimax_key):
77	            _log.info("synced MINIMAX_API_KEY into openclaw auth profiles")
78	    else:
79	        _log.info("MINIMAX_API_KEY not set; openclaw MiniMax tiers stay unauthenticated")
80	
81	
82	def provision_copilot(home: Path, model: str | None) -> None:
83	    src = _ASSETS / "copilot" / "settings.json"
84	    if not src.is_file():
85	        _log.warning("bundled copilot settings missing at %s", src)
86	        return
87	    dst_dir = home / ".copilot"
88	    dst_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
89	    dst = dst_dir / "settings.json"
90	    if not dst.exists():
91	        settings = json.loads(src.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
92	        if model:
93	            settings["model"] = model
94	        dst.write_text(json.dumps(settings, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n",
95	                       encoding="utf-8")
96	
97	
98	def provision_skills(home: Path, skills_dir: Path | None) -> None:
99	    """Share the project skills with both agent backends (single source of truth)."""
100	    if not skills_dir or not skills_dir.is_dir():
101	        return
102	    for dest in (home / ".copilot" / "skills", home / ".openclaw" / "workspace" / "skills"):
103	        _copy_tree(skills_dir, dest)
104	
105	
106	def provision(
107	    *,
108	    home: Path | None = None,
109	    minimax_key: str | None = None,
110	    copilot_model: str | None = None,
111	    skills_dir: Path | None = None,
112	) -> None:
113	    home = home or Path(os.environ.get("HOME", "/root"))
114	    provision_openclaw(home, minimax_key)
115	    provision_copilot(home, copilot_model)
116	    provision_skills(home, skills_dir)
117	
118	
119	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
120	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Provision agent-fix backend config")
121	    parser.add_argument("--home", default=None, help="target home (default: $HOME)")
122	    parser.add_argument("--minimax-env", default="MINIMAX_API_KEY",
123	                        help="env var holding the MiniMax API key")
124	    parser.add_argument("--copilot-model", default=None,
125	                        help="override the copilot settings.json model")
126	    parser.add_argument("--skills-dir", default=None,
127	                        help="project skills dir to share with both backends")
128	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
129	    provision(
130	        home=Path(args.home) if args.home else None,
131	        minimax_key=os.environ.get(args.minimax_env) or None,
132	        copilot_model=args.copilot_model,
133	        skills_dir=Path(args.skills_dir) if args.skills_dir else None,
134	    )
135	    _log.info("agent backend config provisioned")
136	    return 0
137	
138	
139	if __name__ == "__main__":
140	    raise SystemExit(main())

1	"""Invoke the agent CLI (OpenClaw / Copilot) to attempt a fix.
2	
3	Ports ``run_openclaw_fix`` / ``run_copilot_fix`` from
4	``local_dispatch/agent/agent_backends.sh``.  Each backend runs a headless,
5	tool-enabled agent against the working tree with a timeout; the combined output
6	is written to ``log_path`` for :mod:`aqa.agent.verdict` to parse.
7	
8	Auth is env-var only: OpenClaw reads ``MINIMAX_API_KEY``; Copilot uses BYOK
9	(reusing ``MINIMAX_API_KEY``) or ``COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN``.  Nothing is inlined.
10	"""

113	def _copilot_fix(prompt: str, log_path: Path, session_id: str, tier: Tier,
114	                 timeout: int, workdir: Path) -> int:
115	    if shutil.which("copilot") is None:
116	        raise AgentUnavailable("copilot CLI not found")
117	    env = {**os.environ, **tier.env}
118	    byok = tier.byok or bool(env.get("COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL") or env.get("COPILOT_MINIMAX"))
119	    if byok:

129	    cli_session_id = _copilot_session_id(session_id)

131	    # attempt log so they upload with the results; --session-id ties the run to the
132	    # session-state we archive afterwards.
133	    share_md = log_path.with_name(f"{log_path.stem}.share.md")
134	    copilot_logs = log_path.with_name(f"{log_path.stem}_copilot_logs")
135	    cmd = [

137	        "--session-id", cli_session_id,
138	        "--share", str(share_md),

145	    for d in (str(workdir), str(log_path.parent), os.environ.get("HOME", "/root"),
146	              "/opt", "/usr", "/tmp"):
147	        cmd += ["--add-dir", d]

149	        cmd += ["--model", tier.model]
150	    _log.info("copilot agent (session=%s, byok=%s, model=%s, timeout=%ss)",
151	              cli_session_id, byok, tier.model or "default", timeout)
152	    rc = _run(cmd, log_path, timeout, env)
153	    _archive_agent_session("copilot", cli_session_id, log_path, env)
154	    return rc

158	                  session_id: str | None = None, workdir: Path | None = None,
159	                  timeout: int = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT) -> int:

162	    Raises :class:`AgentUnavailable` if the backend CLI is missing or unauthenticated

1	"""Capture agent source edits as unified-diff patches.
2	
3	Ports ``local_dispatch/agent/patch_capture.sh``.  Before the fix-loop makes any
4	edit we snapshot the *editable areas* (the installed ``auto_round`` / ``vllm``
5	package source + the HF model custom-code cache).  After a fix we diff the live
6	tree against that pristine snapshot to record exactly what the agent changed --
7	uploaded with the results so a fix is reproducible / reviewable.
8	
9	The snapshot + diff are pure filesystem operations (``difflib`` based), so this
10	module is fully testable without any agent or GPU.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import difflib
16	import importlib.util
17	import os
18	import shutil
19	import subprocess
20	from dataclasses import dataclass
21	from pathlib import Path
22	
23	from ..logging_util import get_logger
24	
25	_log = get_logger("agent.patch")
26	
27	# Heavy/binary noise excluded from BOTH snapshot and diff (source edits only).
28	_EXCLUDE_DIRS = {"__pycache__", ".git", "build", "dist", ".mypy_cache", ".pytest_cache"}
29	_EXCLUDE_SUFFIXES = (".pyc", ".pyo", ".so", ".o", ".a", ".bin", ".pt", ".safetensors")
30	
31	
32	@dataclass(frozen=True)
33	class PatchArea:
34	    label: str      # short name used in a/<label> b/<label> headers
35	    category: str   # manifest bucket (auto_round | vllm | model_code)
36	    path: Path      # live directory on disk
37	
38	
39	def _package_dir(name: str) -> Path | None:
40	    try:
41	        spec = importlib.util.find_spec(name)
42	    except (ImportError, ModuleNotFoundError, ValueError):
43	        return None
44	    if spec and spec.submodule_search_locations:
45	        return Path(os.path.realpath(next(iter(spec.submodule_search_locations))))
46	    return None
47	
48	
49	def _hf_modules_dir() -> Path | None:
50	    hf = os.environ.get("HF_HOME") or str(Path(os.environ.get("HOME", "/root")) / ".cache" / "huggingface")
51	    p = Path(hf) / "modules" / "transformers_modules"
52	    return p if p.is_dir() else None
53	
54	
55	def find_editable_areas(*, track_vllm: bool = True) -> list[PatchArea]:
56	    """Discover the source trees an agent fix may edit (present ones only)."""
57	    areas: list[PatchArea] = []
58	    ar = _package_dir("auto_round")
59	    if ar and ar.is_dir():
60	        areas.append(PatchArea("auto_round", "auto_round", ar))
61	    if track_vllm:
62	        vl = _package_dir("vllm")
63	        if vl and vl.is_dir():
64	            areas.append(PatchArea("vllm", "vllm", vl))
65	    hf = _hf_modules_dir()
66	    if hf:
67	        areas.append(PatchArea("model_code", "model_code", hf))
68	    return areas
69	
70	
71	def _keep(path: Path) -> bool:
72	    if path.suffix in _EXCLUDE_SUFFIXES:
73	        return False
74	    return not any(part in _EXCLUDE_DIRS for part in path.parts)
75	
76	
77	def _ignore(_dir: str, names: list[str]) -> set[str]:
78	    out = set()
79	    for n in names:
80	        if n in _EXCLUDE_DIRS or n.endswith(_EXCLUDE_SUFFIXES):
81	            out.add(n)
82	    return out
83	
84	
85	def _read_lines(path: Path) -> list[str]:
86	    try:
87	        return path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines(keepends=True)
88	    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
89	        return []
90	
91	
92	class PatchCapture:
93	    """Snapshot editable areas, then produce unified diffs of the agent's edits."""
94	
95	    def __init__(self, snapshot_root: Path, *, track_vllm: bool = True,
96	                 areas: list[PatchArea] | None = None):
97	        self.snapshot_root = Path(snapshot_root)
98	        self.track_vllm = track_vllm
99	        self.areas: list[PatchArea] = areas if areas is not None else []
100	        self._snapped: set[str] = set()
101	
102	    def snapshot(self) -> int:
103	        """Copy every discovered (or provided) editable area to the pristine root.
104	
105	        Idempotent per area: an already-snapshotted area is never overwritten, so a
106	        late call (after packages install) captures new areas without clobbering
107	        baselines -- mirrors ``patch_snapshot_ensure``.
108	        """
109	        self.snapshot_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
110	        if not self.areas:
111	            self.areas = find_editable_areas(track_vllm=self.track_vllm)
112	        added = 0
113	        for area in self.areas:
114	            if area.label in self._snapped:
115	                continue
116	            dst = self.snapshot_root / area.label
117	            if dst.exists():
118	                self._snapped.add(area.label)
119	                continue
120	            try:
121	                shutil.copytree(area.path, dst, ignore=_ignore, dirs_exist_ok=True)
122	                self._snapped.add(area.label)
123	                added += 1
124	            except (OSError, shutil.Error) as exc:
125	                _log.warning("patch: snapshot of %s failed: %s", area.label, exc)
126	        if added:
127	            _log.info("patch: snapshotted %d editable area(s)", added)
128	        return added
129	
130	    def _area_diff(self, area: PatchArea) -> str:
131	        snap = self.snapshot_root / area.label
132	        if not snap.is_dir() or not area.path.is_dir():
133	            return ""
134	        chunks: list[str] = []
135	        cur_files = {p.relative_to(area.path): p for p in area.path.rglob("*")
136	                     if p.is_file() and _keep(p)}
137	        snap_files = {p.relative_to(snap): p for p in snap.rglob("*")
138	                      if p.is_file() and _keep(p)}
139	        for rel in sorted(set(cur_files) | set(snap_files), key=str):
140	            old = _read_lines(snap_files[rel]) if rel in snap_files else []
141	            new = _read_lines(cur_files[rel]) if rel in cur_files else []
142	            if old == new:
143	                continue
144	            diff = difflib.unified_diff(
145	                old, new,
146	                fromfile=f"a/{area.label}/{rel}",
147	                tofile=f"b/{area.label}/{rel}",
148	            )
149	            chunks.append("".join(diff))
150	        return "".join(chunks)
151	
152	    def combined_diff(self) -> str:
153	        """Unified diff across all tracked areas (empty if nothing changed)."""
154	        return "".join(self._area_diff(a) for a in self.areas)
155	
156	    def write_patches(self, out_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Path]:
157	        """Write a per-area patch + a combined patch under ``out_dir``; return the paths."""
158	        out_dir = Path(out_dir)
159	        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
160	        written: dict[str, Path] = {}
161	        combined_parts: list[str] = []
162	        for area in self.areas:
163	            d = self._area_diff(area)
164	            if not d:
165	                continue
166	            p = out_dir / f"{area.label}.patch"
167	            p.write_text(d)
168	            written[area.label] = p
169	            combined_parts.append(d)
170	        if combined_parts:
171	            combined = out_dir / "combined.patch"
172	            combined.write_text("".join(combined_parts))
173	            written["combined"] = combined
174	        return written
175	
176	    # -- deterministic replay (apply a *recorded* patch, revert on failure) ----
177	    def _area_by_label(self, label: str) -> PatchArea | None:
178	        for area in self.areas:
179	            if area.label == label:
180	                return area
181	        return None
182	
183	    def apply_recorded(self, patch_by_label: dict[str, Path]) -> bool:
184	        """Apply recorded per-area ``.patch`` files onto the live tree.
185	
186	        Each label must map to a currently-tracked area; the diff was written with
187	        ``a/<label>/<rel>`` headers, so ``patch -p2`` (strip ``a/`` + ``<label>/``)
188	        applies it relative to the area dir. We dry-run *every* patch first and only
189	        commit if all apply cleanly -- an all-or-nothing atomic replay. A patch that
190	        doesn't apply (different package version, model family, ...) is a normal miss,
191	        not an error: we return ``False`` and the caller escalates to the agent.
192	        """
193	        if shutil.which("patch") is None:
194	            _log.info("replay: `patch` tool unavailable; skipping deterministic replay")
195	            return False
196	        targets: list[tuple[PatchArea, Path]] = []
197	        for label, patch_file in patch_by_label.items():
198	            if label == "combined":
199	                continue
200	            area = self._area_by_label(label)
201	            pf = Path(patch_file)
202	            if area is None or not area.path.is_dir() or not pf.is_file() or pf.stat().st_size == 0:
203	                return False
204	            targets.append((area, pf))
205	        if not targets:
206	            return False
207	        # Phase 1: dry-run everything.
208	        for area, pf in targets:
209	            if not self._patch(area.path, pf, dry_run=True):
210	                return False
211	        # Phase 2: commit (revert-all if any step unexpectedly fails).
212	        applied: list[PatchArea] = []
213	        for area, pf in targets:
214	            if self._patch(area.path, pf, dry_run=False):
215	                applied.append(area)
216	            else:
217	                self.restore()
218	                return False
219	        _log.info("replay: applied recorded patch to %d area(s): %s",
220	                  len(applied), ", ".join(a.label for a in applied))
221	        return True
222	
223	    @staticmethod
224	    def _patch(area_path: Path, patch_file: Path, *, dry_run: bool) -> bool:
225	        cmd = ["patch", "-p2", "--forward", "--no-backup-if-mismatch",
226	               "-d", str(area_path), "-i", str(patch_file)]
227	        if dry_run:
228	            cmd.append("--dry-run")
229	        try:
230	            rc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True,
231	                                timeout=120, check=False).returncode
232	        except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
233	            _log.warning("replay: patch invocation failed: %s", exc)
234	            return False
235	        return rc == 0
236	
237	    def restore(self) -> int:
238	        """Revert every tracked area to its pristine snapshot (undo agent/replay edits).
239	
240	        Used after a failed replay (or a fix that must be rolled back) so the next
241	        attempt starts from a clean tree. Only snapshotted areas are restored.
242	        """
243	        restored = 0
244	        for area in self.areas:
245	            snap = self.snapshot_root / area.label
246	            if not snap.is_dir():
247	                continue
248	            try:
249	                if area.path.exists():
250	                    shutil.rmtree(area.path, ignore_errors=True)
251	                shutil.copytree(snap, area.path, ignore=_ignore, dirs_exist_ok=True)
252	                restored += 1
253	            except (OSError, shutil.Error) as exc:
254	                _log.warning("restore of %s failed: %s", area.label, exc)
255	        if restored:
256	            _log.info("replay: restored %d area(s) to pristine snapshot", restored)
257	        return restored

16	# same underlying error classifies identically across attempts (drift stability).
17	#
18	# Ordering matters: put SPECIFIC patterns before generic ones so, e.g., a CUDA OOM
19	# classifies as ``oom`` (not the generic ``runtime_error`` its RuntimeError wrapper
20	# would otherwise match). Categories are intentionally fine-grained: a coarse class

25	                       r"CUDA error: out of memory", re.IGNORECASE)),
26	    ("cpu_oom", re.compile(r"DefaultCPUAllocator: can't allocate|"
27	                           r"Cannot allocate memory|std::bad_alloc|Killed\b.*memory",
28	                           re.IGNORECASE)),
29	    ("disk_space", re.compile(r"No space left on device|OSError: \[Errno 28\]|"
30	                              r"Disk quota exceeded", re.IGNORECASE)),
31	    # -- tensor / numeric layout ----------------------------------------------

33	                                  r"mat1 and mat2|must match the size|"
34	                                  r"expected .* but got .* shape|"
35	                                  r"The size of tensor .* must match", re.IGNORECASE)),
36	    ("dtype_mismatch", re.compile(r"expected .* dtype|Input type .* and weight type|"
37	                                  r"promote|got Half|got BFloat16|mixed dtype|"
38	                                  r"expected scalar type|can't convert .* dtype", re.IGNORECASE)),
39	    ("nan_inf", re.compile(r"\bNaN\b|\bInf\b|not finite|loss is nan|"
40	                           r"probability tensor contains", re.IGNORECASE)),
41	    ("meta_device_error", re.compile(r"meta device|Cannot copy out of meta tensor|"
42	                                     r"to_empty\(\)|on the meta device", re.IGNORECASE)),
43	    # -- CUDA runtime / kernels ------------------------------------------------
44	    ("cuda_unavailable", re.compile(r"CUDA .*not available|no CUDA-capable device|"

57	    ("checkpoint_key_mismatch", re.compile(r"Missing key|Unexpected key|"
58	                                           r"Error\(s\) in loading state_dict|"
59	                                           r"size of tensor .* must match", re.IGNORECASE)),
60	    ("tokenizer_error", re.compile(r"tokenizer|SentencePiece|added_tokens|"
61	                                   r"vocab_size|chat[_ ]template", re.IGNORECASE)),
62	    # -- dependency / environment ---------------------------------------------
63	    ("import_error", re.compile(r"ModuleNotFoundError|ImportError|No module named|"
64	                                r"cannot import name|undefined symbol|"
65	                                r"version .* GLIBC", re.IGNORECASE)),
66	    ("permission_error", re.compile(r"PermissionError|Permission denied|"
67	                                    r"\[Errno 13\]", re.IGNORECASE)),
68	    # -- serving / inference engine -------------------------------------------
69	    ("vllm_engine_error", re.compile(r"EngineCore|AsyncLLMEngine|Engine core initialization|"
70	                                     r"engine .* died|RayWorker|vllm.*Error", re.IGNORECASE)),
71	    # -- network / download (transient vs permanent split) --------------------
72	    ("auth_error", re.compile(r"401 Client Error|403 Client Error|"
73	                              r"Repository Not Found|GatedRepo|"
74	                              r"Invalid.*token|Unauthorized", re.IGNORECASE)),
75	    ("download_missing", re.compile(r"Entry Not Found|404 Client Error|"
76	                                    r"EntryNotFound|does not appear to have a file", re.IGNORECASE)),
77	    ("network_transient", re.compile(r"Connection .*refused|Connection reset|"
78	                                     r"Read timed out|ConnectionError|"
79	                                     r"Max retries exceeded|Temporary failure|"
80	                                     r"ReadTimeout|502 |503 |504 ", re.IGNORECASE)),
81	    # -- generic Python exception classes (last-resort buckets) ---------------
82	    ("key_error", re.compile(r"\bKeyError\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
83	    ("index_error", re.compile(r"\bIndexError\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
84	    ("type_error", re.compile(r"\bTypeError\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
85	    ("attribute_error", re.compile(r"\bAttributeError\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
86	    ("assertion_error", re.compile(r"\bAssertionError\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
87	    ("value_error", re.compile(r"\bValueError\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
88	    ("runtime_error", re.compile(r"\bRuntimeError\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
89	]
90	
91	# Deepest exception CLASS name in a traceback (Harbor-style structured signal):
92	# ``...\nSomeModule.SomeError: message`` -> ``SomeError``. Precise and maintenance-free,
93	# it complements the semantic taxonomy above (which groups synonyms like a CUDA OOM
94	# RuntimeError and OutOfMemoryError into one ``oom`` category).
95	_EXC_TYPE_RE = re.compile(
96	    r"^[\s>*\-]*(?:[A-Za-z_][\w.]*\.)?"          # optional module path prefix
97	    r"([A-Za-z_]\w*(?:Error|Exception|Warning|Interrupt|Timeout))\s*:",
98	    re.MULTILINE,
99	)
100	
101	# torch-dynamo wraps the true exception as ``raised exception <Name>(...)``; the
102	# deepest colon-form in the traceback is then only a generic RuntimeError wrapper.
103	# Recover the inner class name so replay keys off the real exception type.
104	_DYNAMO_EXC_TYPE_RE = re.compile(
105	    r"raised exception\s+([A-Za-z_][\w.]*(?:Error|Exception))\("
106	)
107	
108	# Volatile, non-error chatter dropped before classification/similarity so the same
109	# crash looks the same across attempts.
110	_VOLATILE = re.compile(
111	    r"A new version of the following files was downloaded|"
112	    r"Make sure to double-check|"
113	    r"\d{3,} Client Error|Entry Not Found for url|Request ID: Root=|"
114	    r"You are sending unauthenticated requests|"
115	    r"Generating [\w-]+ split:|"
116	    r"^(Map|Filter|Downloading|Resolving|Loading)[\w ]*:\s*\d+%|"
117	    r"\b\d+%\|[#\u2588\u2589\u258a\u258b\u258c\u258d\u258e\u258f ]*\||"
118	    r"falling back to in-process mode|examples/s\]\s*$"
119	)
120	
121	
122	def _denoise_for_class(text: str) -> str:
123	    lines = [ln for ln in text.splitlines() if not _VOLATILE.search(ln)]
124	    return "\n".join(lines) or text
125	
126	
127	def classify_error(text: str) -> str:
128	    """Return a stable snake_case error category (``unknown`` if nothing matches)."""
129	    cleaned = _denoise_for_class(text or "")
130	    for category, pat in _RULES:
131	        if pat.search(cleaned):
132	            return category
133	    return "unknown"
134	
135	
136	def exception_type(text: str) -> str:
137	    """Deepest Python exception CLASS name in a traceback, or ``""`` if none.
138	
139	    A precise, maintenance-free structured signal (mirrors Harbor's
140	    ``type(e).__name__``): ``RuntimeError: size mismatch`` -> ``RuntimeError``,
141	    ``modeling_qwen.MyError: ...`` -> ``MyError``. Used as a mid-precision replay
142	    key between the exact error signature and the coarse semantic category.
143	    """
144	    cleaned = _denoise_for_class(text or "")
145	    dynamo = _DYNAMO_EXC_TYPE_RE.findall(cleaned)
146	    if dynamo:
147	        name = dynamo[-1]
148	        return name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
149	    matches = _EXC_TYPE_RE.findall(cleaned)
150	    return matches[-1] if matches else ""
151	
152	
153	def _denoise_for_sim(text: str) -> str:
154	    out: list[str] = []
155	    for ln in (text or "").splitlines():
156	        if re.search(r"HTTP Request|HTTP/1\.1|Client Error|Downloading|it/s\]|"
157	                     r"\|\s*\d+/\d+|Config was last written|allowlist contains|"
158	                     r"WARNING logging", ln):
159	            continue
160	        s = re.sub(r"^\S*\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT[\d:.]+Z?\s*", "", ln)
161	        s = re.sub(r"\b\d{1,2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\b", "", s)
162	        s = re.sub(r"\[[A-Z]+\]", "", s)
163	        s = re.sub(r"0x[0-9a-fA-F]+", "0xADDR", s)
164	        s = re.sub(r"/[^\s:]+/", "/PATH/", s)
165	        s = re.sub(r"\d+\.\d+\s?[GMK]i?B", "SIZE", s)
166	        s = re.sub(r"line \d+", "line N", s)
167	        s = re.sub(r"\d+", "N", s)
168	        s = s.strip()
169	        if s:
170	            out.append(s)
171	    return "\n".join(out)
172	
173	
174	def logs_similarity(a: str, b: str) -> float | None:
175	    """Denoised difflib ratio of two error logs, or None if either is empty."""
176	    da, db = _denoise_for_sim(a), _denoise_for_sim(b)
177	    if not da or not db:
178	        return None
179	    return difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, da, db).ratio()
180	
181	
182	def extract_progress(text: str) -> int:
183	    """Deepest ``layers.<N>`` index seen in a log (proxy for how far quant got); -1 if none."""
184	    nums = [int(m) for m in re.findall(r"layers\.(\d+)", text or "")]
185	    return max(nums) if nums else -1

1	"""Parse structured fields and the verdict from an agent's fix-attempt output.
2	
3	Ports the ``agent_verdict`` / ``extract_agent_field`` logic from
4	``local_dispatch/agent/agent_fix_loop.sh``.  The parsing is deliberately strict:
5	only a line whose ``VERDICT:`` value is exactly one of the tokens counts, so prose
6	like *"Only declare VERDICT: UNFIXABLE for ..."* or the placeholder
7	``VERDICT: <FIXABLE | ...>`` is ignored.
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import re
13	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
14	from enum import Enum
15	
16	
17	class Verdict(str, Enum):
18	    FIXABLE = "fixable"
19	    UNFIXABLE = "unfixable"
20	    ESCALATE = "escalate"
21	
22	
23	# A real verdict line: optional markdown/bullets, VERDICT:, EXACTLY one token, EOL.
24	_VERDICT_RE = re.compile(
25	    r"^[\s>*\-]*VERDICT\s*:?\s*\**\s*(FIXABLE|UNFIXABLE|ESCALATE)\s*\.?\**\s*$",
26	    re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE,
27	)
28	
29	# The single-line labels the protocol asks the agent to emit.
30	_LABELS = (
31	    "COMPONENT",
32	    "ERROR_CLASS",
33	    "ROOT_CAUSE_HYPOTHESIS",
34	    "EVIDENCE_CMD",
35	    "EVIDENCE_RESULT",
36	    "VERDICT",
37	    "UNFIXABLE_REASON",
38	    "FIX_TIER",
39	    "FIX_PLAN",
40	    "SMOKE_TEST",
41	)
42	
43	
44	def parse_verdict(text: str) -> Verdict | None:
45	    """Return the LAST valid verdict in ``text`` (later attempts override), or None.
46	
47	    Placeholder lines (``VERDICT: <FIXABLE | UNFIXABLE | ESCALATE>``) never match
48	    because the captured group would have to be a single bare token.
49	    """
50	    matches = _VERDICT_RE.findall(text or "")
51	    if not matches:
52	        return None
53	    return Verdict(matches[-1].lower())
54	
55	
56	def extract_field(text: str, label: str, max_len: int = 200) -> str:
57	    """Pull a labeled single-line field's value (last occurrence wins)."""
58	    if not text:
59	        return ""
60	    pat = re.compile(
61	        rf"^[\s>*\-]*{re.escape(label)}\s*:?\s*\**\s*(.+?)\s*\**\s*$",
62	        re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE,
63	    )
64	    values = [m.group(1).strip() for m in pat.finditer(text)]
65	    # Drop placeholder values like "<ONE stable snake_case token ...>".
66	    values = [v for v in values if not (v.startswith("<") and v.endswith(">"))]
67	    if not values:
68	        return ""
69	    return values[-1][:max_len]
70	
71	
72	def _normalize_class(raw: str) -> str:
73	    """Normalize an ERROR_CLASS token to a stable snake_case identifier."""
74	    tok = raw.strip().split()[0] if raw.strip() else ""
75	    tok = tok.lower()
76	    tok = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9_]", "", tok)
77	    return tok
78	
79	
80	@dataclass
81	class AgentAnalysis:
82	    """Structured view of one agent fix attempt's output."""
83	
84	    verdict: Verdict | None = None
85	    component: str = ""
86	    error_class: str = ""
87	    root_cause: str = ""
88	    unfixable_reason: str = ""
89	    fix_tier: str = ""
90	    fix_plan: str = ""
91	    smoke_test: str = ""
92	    raw: str = field(default="", repr=False)
93	
94	    @classmethod
95	    def parse(cls, text: str) -> AgentAnalysis:
96	        return cls(
97	            verdict=parse_verdict(text),
98	            component=extract_field(text, "COMPONENT", 60),
99	            error_class=_normalize_class(extract_field(text, "ERROR_CLASS", 60)),
100	            root_cause=extract_field(text, "ROOT_CAUSE_HYPOTHESIS", 400),
101	            unfixable_reason=extract_field(text, "UNFIXABLE_REASON", 200),
102	            fix_tier=extract_field(text, "FIX_TIER", 40),
103	            fix_plan=extract_field(text, "FIX_PLAN", 400),
104	            smoke_test=extract_field(text, "SMOKE_TEST", 400),
105	            raw=text or "",
106	        )
107	
108	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
109	        d = {
110	            "verdict": self.verdict.value if self.verdict else None,
111	            "component": self.component,
112	            "error_class": self.error_class,
113	            "root_cause": self.root_cause,
114	            "unfixable_reason": self.unfixable_reason,
115	            "fix_tier": self.fix_tier,
116	            "fix_plan": self.fix_plan,
117	            "smoke_test": self.smoke_test,
118	        }
119	        return {k: v for k, v in d.items() if v}

1	"""OpenAI-compatible async model client for endpoint-centric (agentic) evaluation.
2	
3	Ports the role of NeMo Evaluator's ``ModelClient``: a thin async client that talks
4	to an OpenAI-compatible ``/v1/chat/completions`` (+ ``/v1/completions``) endpoint --
5	e.g. a quantized model served by ``vllm serve``.  Unlike the lm_eval subprocess
6	path, agentic/terminal benchmarks drive the model as a *served endpoint*, so a
7	solver can hold a multi-turn conversation.
8	
9	The HTTP POST is delegated to an injectable ``transport`` coroutine so the client
10	(and everything above it) is unit-testable with no server and no httpx.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import asyncio
16	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
17	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
18	from typing import Any
19	
20	from ..logging_util import AqaError, get_logger
21	
22	_log = get_logger("agent_eval.client")
23	
24	# transport(url, payload, headers) -> decoded JSON response dict.
25	Transport = Callable[[str, dict, dict], Awaitable[dict]]
26	
27	
28	async def _httpx_transport(url: str, payload: dict, headers: dict) -> dict:
29	    """Default transport: POST JSON via httpx (lazily imported)."""
30	    try:
31	        import httpx
32	    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - exercised only without httpx
33	        raise AqaError("httpx is required for the live endpoint transport; "
34	                       "`pip install autoquant-agent[agent]`") from exc
35	    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=None) as client:
36	        resp = await client.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
37	        resp.raise_for_status()
38	        return resp.json()
39	
40	
41	@dataclass
42	class ModelClient:
43	    """Async OpenAI-compatible client (chat + completion) for a served model."""
44	
45	    base_url: str
46	    model: str
47	    api_key: str | None = None
48	    timeout: float = 300.0
49	    max_retries: int = 2
50	    default_params: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
51	    transport: Transport | None = None
52	
53	    def _url(self, path: str) -> str:
54	        base = self.base_url.rstrip("/")
55	        if not base.endswith("/v1"):
56	            base = base + "/v1"
57	        return f"{base}/{path.lstrip('/')}"
58	
59	    def _headers(self) -> dict[str, str]:
60	        h = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
61	        if self.api_key:
62	            h["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {self.api_key}"
63	        return h
64	
65	    async def _post(self, url: str, payload: dict) -> dict:
66	        transport = self.transport or _httpx_transport
67	        last: Exception | None = None
68	        for attempt in range(self.max_retries + 1):
69	            try:
70	                return await asyncio.wait_for(
71	                    transport(url, payload, self._headers()), timeout=self.timeout)
72	            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - retry any transport error
73	                last = exc
74	                if attempt < self.max_retries:
75	                    await asyncio.sleep(0.5 * (attempt + 1))
76	                    _log.warning("endpoint POST retry %d: %s", attempt + 1, exc)
77	        raise AqaError(f"endpoint request failed after {self.max_retries + 1} tries: {last}")
78	
79	    async def chat(self, messages: list[dict[str, str]], **params: Any) -> str:
80	        """Call ``/chat/completions`` and return the assistant message content."""
81	        content, _ = await self.chat_with_usage(messages, **params)
82	        return content
83	
84	    async def chat_with_usage(
85	        self, messages: list[dict[str, str]], **params: Any
86	    ) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]:
87	        """Like :meth:`chat` but also return the response ``usage`` block.
88	
89	        The usage dict is passed straight through from the endpoint (empty when
90	        the server omits it) so callers can fold it into a
91	        :class:`~aqa.agent_eval.stats.TokenStats`.
92	        """
93	        payload = {"model": self.model, "messages": messages,
94	                   **self.default_params, **params}
95	        data = await self._post(self._url("chat/completions"), payload)
96	        content = data["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
97	        return content, (data.get("usage") or {})
98	
99	    async def complete(self, prompt: str, **params: Any) -> str:
100	        """Call ``/completions`` and return the generated text."""
101	        payload = {"model": self.model, "prompt": prompt,
102	                   **self.default_params, **params}
103	        data = await self._post(self._url("completions"), payload)
104	        return data["choices"][0]["text"]

1	"""Serve a (quantized) model as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint via ``vllm serve``.
2	
3	E0 base for agentic/terminal evaluation: those benchmarks need the model behind a
4	live ``/v1/chat/completions`` endpoint (so a solver can hold multi-turn
5	conversations), not the lm_eval subprocess path.  :class:`VllmEndpoint` launches
6	``vllm serve``, waits for ``/health``, and tears the server down on exit.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import shutil
12	import socket
13	import subprocess
14	import time
15	import urllib.request
16	from pathlib import Path
17	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
18	
19	from ..logging_util import AqaError, get_logger
20	
21	if TYPE_CHECKING:
22	    from typing import Self
23	
24	_log = get_logger("agent_eval.endpoint")
25	
26	
27	def _free_port() -> int:
28	    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
29	        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
30	        return s.getsockname()[1]
31	
32	
33	class VllmEndpoint:
34	    """Launch and manage a ``vllm serve`` OpenAI-compatible server as a context manager."""
35	
36	    def __init__(
37	        self,
38	        model: str,
39	        *,
40	        served_name: str | None = None,
41	        host: str = "127.0.0.1",
42	        port: int | None = None,
43	        num_gpus: int = 1,
44	        extra_args: list[str] | None = None,
45	        startup_timeout: float = 900.0,
46	        log_path: Path | None = None,
47	    ):
48	        self.model = model
49	        self.served_name = served_name or model
50	        self.host = host
51	        self.port = port or _free_port()
52	        self.num_gpus = num_gpus
53	        self.extra_args = list(extra_args or [])
54	        self.startup_timeout = startup_timeout
55	        self.log_path = log_path
56	        self._proc: subprocess.Popen | None = None
57	        self._log_fh = None
58	
59	    @staticmethod
60	    def available() -> bool:
61	        return shutil.which("vllm") is not None
62	
63	    @property
64	    def base_url(self) -> str:
65	        return f"http://{self.host}:{self.port}/v1"
66	
67	    def build_argv(self) -> list[str]:
68	        argv = [
69	            "vllm", "serve", self.model,
70	            "--host", self.host, "--port", str(self.port),
71	            "--served-model-name", self.served_name,
72	        ]
73	        if self.num_gpus > 1:
74	            argv += ["--tensor-parallel-size", str(self.num_gpus)]
75	        argv += self.extra_args
76	        return argv
77	
78	    def _health_url(self) -> str:
79	        return f"http://{self.host}:{self.port}/health"
80	
81	    def _healthy(self) -> bool:
82	        try:
83	            with urllib.request.urlopen(self._health_url(), timeout=2) as resp:
84	                return 200 <= resp.status < 300
85	        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - not up yet
86	            return False
87	
88	    def start(self) -> Self:
89	        if not self.available():
90	            raise AqaError("vllm is not installed; `pip install vllm`")
91	        argv = self.build_argv()
92	        _log.info("[CMD] %s", " ".join(argv))
93	        if self.log_path:
94	            self.log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
95	            self._log_fh = self.log_path.open("w")
96	            out = self._log_fh
97	        else:
98	            out = subprocess.DEVNULL
99	        self._proc = subprocess.Popen(argv, stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
100	        self._await_ready()
101	        return self
102	
103	    def _await_ready(self) -> None:
104	        deadline = time.time() + self.startup_timeout
105	        while time.time() < deadline:
106	            if self._proc and self._proc.poll() is not None:
107	                raise AqaError(f"vllm serve exited early (rc={self._proc.returncode}); "
108	                               f"see {self.log_path}")
109	            if self._healthy():
110	                _log.info("endpoint ready at %s", self.base_url)
111	                return
112	            time.sleep(2.0)
113	        self.stop()
114	        raise AqaError(f"vllm serve not ready within {self.startup_timeout}s")
115	
116	    def stop(self) -> None:
117	        if self._proc and self._proc.poll() is None:
118	            self._proc.terminate()
119	            try:
120	                self._proc.wait(timeout=30)
121	            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
122	                self._proc.kill()
123	        self._proc = None
124	        if self._log_fh:
125	            self._log_fh.close()
126	            self._log_fh = None
127	
128	    def __enter__(self) -> Self:
129	        return self.start()
130	
131	    def __exit__(self, *exc) -> None:
132	        self.stop()

1	"""Solvers: turn a task into a model response via the served endpoint.
2	
3	Ports the role of NeMo Evaluator's ``solvers/`` (chat / completion) at the E0 base
4	level.  A solver owns *how* the model is prompted for a task -- the simplest are
5	:class:`ChatSolver` (single chat turn with an optional system prompt) and
6	:class:`CompletionSolver`.  Richer agentic solvers (tool-use / ReAct / gym) build
7	on the same :class:`Solver` protocol in later phases.
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
13	from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable
14	
15	from .client import ModelClient
16	
17	
18	@dataclass
19	class Task:
20	    """One agentic-eval task."""
21	
22	    id: str
23	    prompt: str
24	    target: str = ""
25	    system: str | None = None
26	    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
27	
28	
29	@runtime_checkable
30	class Solver(Protocol):
31	    async def solve(self, task: Task) -> str:
32	        """Produce the model's answer for ``task``."""
33	        ...
34	
35	
36	@dataclass
37	class ChatSolver:
38	    """Single-turn chat solver (optional per-solver system prompt)."""
39	
40	    client: ModelClient
41	    system: str | None = None
42	    params: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
43	
44	    async def solve(self, task: Task) -> str:
45	        messages: list[dict[str, str]] = []
46	        system = task.system or self.system
47	        if system:
48	            messages.append({"role": "system", "content": system})
49	        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": task.prompt})
50	        return await self.client.chat(messages, **self.params)
51	
52	
53	@dataclass
54	class CompletionSolver:
55	    """Raw text-completion solver (no chat template)."""
56	
57	    client: ModelClient
58	    params: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
59	
60	    async def solve(self, task: Task) -> str:
61	        return await self.client.complete(task.prompt, **self.params)

1	"""ReAct / tool-use solver: drive the model through a multi-turn act loop.
2	
3	Where :class:`~aqa.agent_eval.solver.ChatSolver` answers in one turn, a tool-use
4	agent *acts*: it emits a shell command, the :class:`~aqa.agent_eval.environment`
5	executes it, the observation is fed back, and the loop repeats until the model
6	declares a final answer or the turn budget is exhausted.  This is the classic
7	ReAct loop, and the base an E4 terminal benchmark is scored on.
8	
9	The action protocol is text-based (portable across any served model, no function
10	-calling schema required):
11	
12	  * a fenced `````bash`` / `````sh`` / ``````` block  -> run it as a command;
13	  * a ``Final Answer: ...`` line                       -> finish;
14	  * anything else                                      -> treated as the answer.
15	
16	The resulting :class:`Trajectory` carries the transcript, the final answer, and
17	the environment's terminal reward.  :func:`run_tool_use_eval` aggregates
18	trajectories into the same :class:`~aqa.agent_eval.loop.AgentEvalResult` used by
19	the single-turn path (so ``per_sample`` feeds the statistical gate identically).
20	"""
21	
22	from __future__ import annotations
23	
24	import asyncio
25	import re
26	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
27	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable
28	
29	from ..logging_util import get_logger
30	from .loop import AgentEvalResult, TaskOutcome
31	from .solver import Task
32	from .stats import TokenStats
33	from .verifier import EvalVerdict, Verifier, coerce_verdict, verdict_from_exception
34	
35	if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover
36	    from collections.abc import Callable
37	
38	    from .environment import Environment
39	
40	_log = get_logger("agent_eval.react")
41	
42	
43	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
44	# Action parsing
45	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
46	@dataclass
47	class Command:
48	    """The agent wants to run a shell command."""
49	
50	    cmd: str
51	
52	
53	@dataclass
54	class Finish:
55	    """The agent is done and submits a final answer."""
56	
57	    answer: str
58	
59	
60	Action = Command | Finish
61	
62	_CODE_BLOCK = re.compile(
63	    r"```(?:bash|sh|shell|console)?\s*\n(?P<body>.*?)```",
64	    re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE,
65	)
66	_FINAL = re.compile(r"(?:^|\n)\s*final\s*answer\s*:\s*(?P<ans>.*)", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
67	
68	
69	def parse_action(text: str) -> Action:
70	    """Extract the next action from a model turn (command takes priority)."""
71	    blocks = _CODE_BLOCK.findall(text)
72	    if blocks:
73	        # Use the last fenced block; strip a leading `$ ` prompt if present.
74	        cmd = blocks[-1].strip()
75	        cmd = "\n".join(line.removeprefix("$ ")
76	                        for line in cmd.splitlines()).strip()
77	        if cmd:
78	            return Command(cmd=cmd)
79	    final = _FINAL.search(text)
80	    if final:
81	        return Finish(answer=final.group("ans").strip())
82	    return Finish(answer=text.strip())
83	
84	
85	DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
86	    "You are an autonomous agent solving a task in a Linux shell. "
87	    "Think step by step. To run a command, reply with a single fenced code block:\n"
88	    "```bash\n<command>\n```\n"
89	    "You will then receive its output as an Observation. "
90	    "When the task is complete, reply with a line:\nFinal Answer: <your answer>\n"
91	    "Do not include both a command and a final answer in the same reply."
92	)
93	
94	
95	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
96	# Trajectory
97	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
98	@dataclass
99	class ReActStep:
100	    output: str                     # raw model turn
101	    action: Action
102	    observation: str | None = None  # None for a Finish step
103	
104	
105	@dataclass
106	class Trajectory:
107	    task_id: str
108	    steps: list[ReActStep] = field(default_factory=list)
109	    final_answer: str = ""
110	    solved: bool = False
111	    reward: float = 0.0
112	    hit_turn_limit: bool = False
113	    verdict: EvalVerdict | None = None
114	    stats: TokenStats = field(default_factory=TokenStats)
115	
116	    @property
117	    def turns(self) -> int:
118	        return len(self.steps)
119	
120	
121	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
122	# Agent
123	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
124	@dataclass
125	class ToolUseSolver:
126	    """A ReAct agent driving a model against a per-task :class:`Environment`."""
127	
128	    client: Any                                    # ModelClient / ServingProxy
129	    env_factory: Callable[[Task], Environment]
130	    system_prompt: str = DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT
131	    max_turns: int = 10
132	    params: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
133	    observation_template: str = "Observation:\n{obs}"
134	    verifier: Verifier | None = None
135	
136	    def _initial_user(self, task: Task, obs_text: str) -> str:
137	        parts = [task.prompt]
138	        if obs_text:
139	            parts.append(self.observation_template.format(obs=obs_text))
140	        return "\n\n".join(parts)
141	
142	    async def _terminal_verdict(self, task: Task, traj: Trajectory,
143	                                env: Environment, last: float) -> EvalVerdict:
144	        """Grade the finished trajectory.
145	
146	        Uses the injected :class:`Verifier` when present (structured, may carry
147	        sub-metrics + a failure category); otherwise falls back to the legacy
148	        ``is_solved`` / last-step-reward scalar path, wrapped as a scored verdict.
149	        A verifier that raises is turned into a non-scored (infra/parse) verdict
150	        so a grading crash never masquerades as the model being wrong.
151	        """
152	        if self.verifier is not None:
153	            try:
154	                return await self.verifier.verify(task, traj, env)
155	            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - grading crash != model wrong
156	                _log.warning("verifier failed for %s: %s", task.id, exc)
157	                return verdict_from_exception(exc)
158	        is_solved = getattr(env, "is_solved", None)
159	        if callable(is_solved):
160	            solved = bool(await is_solved())
161	            return EvalVerdict.from_reward(1.0 if solved else 0.0, solved=solved)
162	        return EvalVerdict.from_reward(last, solved=last > 0.0)
163	
164	    async def run(self, task: Task) -> Trajectory:
165	        env = self.env_factory(task)
166	        traj = Trajectory(task_id=task.id)
167	        last_reward = 0.0
168	        try:
169	            first = await env.reset()
170	            messages = [
171	                {"role": "system", "content": self.system_prompt},
172	                {"role": "user", "content": self._initial_user(task, first.text)},
173	            ]
174	            for _ in range(self.max_turns):
175	                output = await self._chat(messages, traj)
176	                messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": output})
177	                action = parse_action(output)
178	                if isinstance(action, Finish):
179	                    traj.steps.append(ReActStep(output, action))
180	                    traj.final_answer = action.answer
181	                    self._settle(traj, await self._terminal_verdict(
182	                        task, traj, env, last_reward))
183	                    break
184	                obs = await env.step(action.cmd)
185	                last_reward = max(last_reward, obs.reward)
186	                traj.steps.append(ReActStep(output, action, obs.text))
187	                messages.append(
188	                    {"role": "user",
189	                     "content": self.observation_template.format(obs=obs.text)}
190	                )
191	                if obs.done:
192	                    self._settle(traj, await self._terminal_verdict(
193	                        task, traj, env, last_reward))
194	                    break
195	            else:
196	                traj.hit_turn_limit = True
197	                self._settle(traj, await self._terminal_verdict(
198	                    task, traj, env, last_reward))
199	        finally:
200	            await env.close()
201	        _log.info("task %s: turns=%d solved=%s reward=%.3f cat=%s tok=%d/%d%s",
202	                  task.id, traj.turns, traj.solved, traj.reward,
203	                  traj.verdict.category if traj.verdict else "-",
204	                  traj.stats.n_input_tokens, traj.stats.n_output_tokens,
205	                  " (turn-limit)" if traj.hit_turn_limit else "")
206	        return traj
207	
208	    @staticmethod
209	    def _settle(traj: Trajectory, verdict: EvalVerdict) -> None:
210	        traj.verdict = verdict
211	        traj.solved = verdict.solved
212	        traj.reward = verdict.reward
213	
214	    async def _chat(self, messages: list[dict[str, str]], traj: Trajectory) -> str:
215	        """One model turn, folding any reported ``usage`` into ``traj.stats``.
216	
217	        Falls back to the plain :meth:`ModelClient.chat` for clients (or fakes)
218	        that predate ``chat_with_usage``, so token accounting is best-effort and
219	        never a hard dependency.
220	        """
221	        with_usage = getattr(self.client, "chat_with_usage", None)
222	        if callable(with_usage):
223	            output, usage = await with_usage(messages, **self.params)
224	            traj.stats.add_usage(usage)
225	            return output
226	        return await self.client.chat(messages, **self.params)
227	
228	    async def solve(self, task: Task) -> str:
229	        """:class:`Solver` adapter -- returns the final answer text."""
230	        return (await self.run(task)).final_answer
231	
232	
233	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
234	# Aggregation
235	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
236	@runtime_checkable
237	class TrajectoryAgent(Protocol):
238	    """Anything that turns a task into a graded :class:`Trajectory`.
239	
240	    Both :class:`ToolUseSolver` and the pluggable scaffolds satisfy this, so the
241	    aggregator below is agent-infra agnostic.
242	    """
243	
244	    async def run(self, task: Task) -> Trajectory: ...
245	
246	
247	async def run_tool_use_eval(
248	    name: str,
249	    tasks: list[Task],
250	    agent: TrajectoryAgent,
251	    *,
252	    concurrency: int = 4,
253	    score_fn: Callable[[Task, Trajectory], float] | None = None,
254	) -> AgentEvalResult:
255	    """Run any trajectory agent over ``tasks`` and aggregate rewards (bounded pool)."""
256	    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(max(1, concurrency))
257	    outcomes: list[TaskOutcome | None] = [None] * len(tasks)
258	
259	    async def _one(idx: int, task: Task) -> None:
260	        async with sem:
261	            try:
262	                traj = await agent.run(task)
263	            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - isolate per-task failures
264	                _log.warning("task %s failed: %s", task.id, exc)
265	                outcomes[idx] = TaskOutcome(
266	                    task.id, "", 0.0, error=str(exc),
267	                    verdict=verdict_from_exception(exc))
268	                return
269	            try:
270	                if score_fn is None:
271	                    score, verdict = traj.reward, traj.verdict
272	                else:
273	                    score = float(score_fn(task, traj))
274	                    verdict = coerce_verdict(score)
275	            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - scoring error is per-task
276	                outcomes[idx] = TaskOutcome(task.id, traj.final_answer, 0.0,
277	                                            error=f"score: {exc}",
278	                                            verdict=verdict_from_exception(exc),
279	                                            stats=traj.stats, turns=traj.turns)
280	                return
281	            outcomes[idx] = TaskOutcome(task.id, traj.final_answer, score,
282	                                        verdict=verdict,
283	                                        stats=traj.stats, turns=traj.turns)
284	
285	    await asyncio.gather(*(_one(i, t) for i, t in enumerate(tasks)))
286	    result = AgentEvalResult(name=name, outcomes=[o for o in outcomes if o is not None])
287	    _log.info("tool-use eval %s: %d tasks, mean=%.4f, errors=%d",
288	              name, result.num_tasks, result.mean_score(),
289	              sum(1 for o in result.outcomes if o.error))
290	    return result
